issues.title: verify-proposal-refs.sh reports BAD LINE RANGE for every .loom/docs/*.md citation (reads the symlink, not the document)
issues.body:
## What happens

`verify-proposal-refs.sh`'s line-range check reads the cited path **through git** (`git show "origin/main:$path" | wc -l`). Since #7842 every `.loom/docs/*.md` with a `defaults/docs/` counterpart is a **symlink** (tree mode `120000`), so that read returns the link-target string, `wc -l` measures the link, and every cited range under `.loom/docs/` is reported as a miss:

```
$ printf 'Cites .loom/docs/troubleshooting.md:100-200\n' > /tmp/probe.md
$ ./.loom/scripts/verify-proposal-refs.sh /tmp/probe.md
verify-proposal-refs.sh: 1 miss(es) in /tmp/probe.md
  - BAD LINE RANGE: `.loom/docs/troubleshooting.md:100-200` — origin/main:.loom/docs/troubleshooting.md has only 0 lines
exit=1
```

The real document has 3031 lines. Because the script **blocks filing** (`hermit.md` / `architect.md`: "Any miss blocks filing"), this pushes proposers away from citing the installed doc paths, or into "fixing" a citation that was correct.

This is the same root cause as #8593 (Champion's premise-false gate reading `.loom/docs/*.md` symlinks through git and closing sound proposals on a check that cannot match). #8593 fixed the Champion side — the prompt rules, `champion-premise-false-evidence.md`'s `resolve_main_path()` recipe, and fixture coverage — and deliberately left this half out: see below.

## Why it was not fixed in #8593's PR

A working shell fix was prototyped in PR #8655 and dropped. It adds ~40 **code** lines to `defaults/scripts/verify-proposal-refs.sh`, which is category `contract` in `scripts/shell-allowlist.txt`, and `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` refuses any growth of the portable pool **with no `Shell-Budget-Growth:` override** (`check_against_rev`: "Portable growth is NOT overridable, deliberately"). Per `.loom/docs/shell-language-policy.md` the correct home for new logic behind a `contract` name is `loom-daemon`.

## Suggested shape

1. A `loom-daemon` verb that resolves a path against a rev — follow a `120000` tree entry to its real blob path (bounded hops; target is relative to the **link's own directory**; normalization must be **lexical**, since the path lives in a commit, not the working tree) and optionally report the resolved blob's line count.
2. `verify-proposal-refs.sh` calls it in the line-range branch, reports the **resolved** path in any `BAD LINE RANGE` message, and reports a dangling link as *unreadable* (e.g. `BROKEN SYMLINK`) rather than "has only 0 lines" — an unreadable file is an inconclusive check, not a disproof (the same distinction #8593 established for Champion).
3. Champion's `resolve_main_path()` snippet (`defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-premise-false-evidence.md`) can then point at the same verb instead of shipping a shell recipe in a prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A body citing an in-range line span under `.loom/docs/` exits 0 (no miss).
- [ ] A genuinely out-of-range span under `.loom/docs/` still misses, and the message names the **resolved** path and the real line count.
- [ ] A dangling symlink is reported as unreadable, not as a 0-line file.
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/tests/test-verify-proposal-refs.sh` gains a symlink fixture covering all three (a draft of these fixtures exists in PR #8655's history).
- [ ] `loom-daemon shell-budget --check` stays at +0 portable growth.

issues.title: Test the #7972 PR-less hold's forge path (apply_prless_hold_label) with the fake-gh harness
issues.body:
## Context

PR #8727 (#7972) added `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/prless_retry.rs`, whose
most consequential action is the **hold** at the threshold:
`apply_prless_hold_label` adds `loom:blocked`, removes `loom:issue`, and posts a
hold notice naming the failure and the count.

## Gap

Every test in that module builds its registry with `config.skip_label_flip = true`
(`prless_retry.rs`, `fn test_registry`). Under that flag `apply_prless_hold_label`
returns `PrlessHoldOutcome::VetoedNoForge` on its first line and never runs — so
the threshold test (`an_always_failing_worker_is_bounded_at_the_threshold`)
asserts only the *in-memory* `held` flag. Measured: `grep -c install_fake_gh
loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/prless_retry.rs` -> `0`.

The forge-visible half of the mechanism is therefore unverified:

- the `gh issue edit --add-label loom:blocked --remove-label loom:issue` argv,
- the closed-issue veto (`issue_is_closed_or_pr(issue) == Some(true)`),
- the open-PR re-verification veto (`probe_open_linked_pr`) and the
  `VetoedOpenPr` -> `clear_prless_retry` path in `record_prless_release`,
- the attempt-note comment posted from the second consecutive release.

## Why it is worth closing

The harness already exists and a sibling mechanism uses it:
`crate::sweep_registry::test_support::install_fake_gh_env_logger`, driven by
`apply_quarantine_label_applies_registered_gh_config_dir`
(`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/quarantine.rs:2505`). The same shape should be
cheap to apply here.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test with `skip_label_flip = false` and a fake `gh` asserts the hold's
      argv contains `--add-label loom:blocked` and `--remove-label loom:issue`
      for the right issue number.
- [ ] A test asserts the hold notice comment is posted and carries
      `PRLESS_RETRY_COMMENT_MARKER`.
- [ ] A test asserts the `VetoedOpenPr` path: re-verification finding an open
      linked PR does not flip labels and clears the tally.
- [ ] A test asserts the closed-issue veto does not flip labels.

Filed by Judge during review of PR #8727 (approved; this is follow-up coverage,
not a defect found in the diff).

issues.title: observability: scheduled transcript archive + local sink (G2 part 1 of #8714)
issues.body:
## Context

Sub-issue of #8714 (slice 3 of 5, "G2 scheduled archive + `local` sink"). Parent issue's own scoping — see #8714 for the full gap analysis. Explicitly independent of the other slices: no egress, no operator decision needed (unlike the sibling `s3`/R2 sink sub-issue, which is gated on D1/D2).

## Problem

Raw transcript archives stay in `~/.loom/transcript-archives` (`activity/transcript_archive.rs`, landed #8494) — but nothing schedules the archive pass. It is opt-in CLI only, with no config block and no scheduler. Claude Code deletes the transcript source at 30 days, so an unscheduled archive pass means archives are only created if someone remembers to run the command by hand before that window closes.

## Proposal

A `transcriptArchive` config block: `enabled`, `intervalSecs`, `minAgeHours`, `archiveDir`, `sinks: [...]` — so the daemon runs the existing archive pass on a schedule. This sub-issue covers the scheduler and the `local` sink only (the archive already lands locally today; this wires it to run unattended and ledgers the result).

Ledger the archive per `(archive, sink)` in `transcript_archive` so a re-run is idempotent — re-running after a partial failure does not re-archive what already succeeded.

The `s3`/R2 remote sink is deliberately **out of scope** for this sub-issue (sibling sub-issue, gated on operator decisions D1/D2 in the parent issue). This sub-issue's `sinks` list has exactly one member, `local`, at completion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `transcriptArchive` config block exists (`enabled`, `intervalSecs`, `minAgeHours`, `archiveDir`, `sinks`), and when `enabled: true`, the daemon runs the existing archive pass on the configured interval without manual CLI invocation.
- [ ] `minAgeHours` is honored — a transcript younger than the threshold is not archived on a given pass.
- [ ] Archive results are ledgered per `(archive, sink)`; re-running the scheduled pass after a partial failure does not re-archive an already-successfully-archived transcript.
- [ ] With only `local` configured in `sinks`, behavior matches today's opt-in CLI archive pass (per #8494), just scheduled instead of manual.
- [ ] No egress occurs from this sub-issue's scope — confirmed by the absence of any network call in the `local`-only code path.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/activity/transcript_archive.rs` — existing archive pass (landed #8494, opt-in CLI only); add the scheduler and config-driven invocation
- Config schema (exact location TBD — wherever other scheduled-task config blocks like `autonomous.*` are declared) — add `transcriptArchive`
- `loom-daemon/src/main.rs` or the daemon's task-scheduling loop (exact location TBD — grep for how other interval-driven background passes, e.g. transcript-ingest's 15-minute cadence, are scheduled) — wire in the new scheduled pass

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: with `transcriptArchive.enabled: true` and a short `intervalSecs`, confirm the archive pass runs without manual invocation
- [ ] Automated tests: `minAgeHours` correctly excludes a transcript younger than the threshold
- [ ] Automated tests: idempotency — re-running after a simulated partial failure does not re-archive a transcript already ledgered as archived to `local`
- [ ] Manual verification: enable the config block on a host with existing transcripts, confirm archives appear in `archiveDir` on schedule with no manual CLI step

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

**Why `routine`, not `complex`**: this wires an existing, already-tested archive pass to a scheduler and a config block — no new egress, no new decision, no new external dependency. The idempotency ledger is the one subtlety, but it is a bounded, testable mechanism, not a judgment call.

## Related

- Parent: #8714 (observability multi-sink export)
- Sibling sub-issue: G2 `s3`/R2 sink (deliberately out of scope here; gated on operator decisions D1/D2)
- #8494 (existing archive pass, landed, reused not rebuilt)

issues.title: observability: session.summary record kind from transcript-ingest (G3 part 1 of #8714)
issues.body:
## Context

Sub-issue of #8714 (slice 2 of 5, "G3 `session.summary`"). Parent issue's own scoping — see #8714 for the full gap analysis. Rides on the multi-exporter sink list (the G1 slice, sibling sub-issue) to actually reach more than one backend, but the record kind itself does not require G1 to have merged first to be implemented — only to be validated end-to-end in both backends per Acceptance below.

## Problem

Transcripts are today read for token counts only (`activity/transcript_ingest.rs`). The only rollups are local SQL views (`cost_by_*`) and the dashboard's token-analytics page. There is no per-session record on the wire at all — nothing carries session-level shape (role, repo, issue, model, turn/tool-call counts) to any exporter.

## Proposal

A new record kind, `session.summary`, emitted by the existing transcript-ingest pass and shipped through whatever exporters are configured (the G1 sink list): one record per transcript (session or subagent), carrying:

- `session_id`, `parent_session_id`
- `runtime`, `role`, `repo`, `issue`, `pr_number`
- `model(s)` used
- four token counters (matching whatever the existing `activity.db` schema already tracks)
- `wall_ms`, `turns`, `tool_calls` (histogram by tool name), `tool_errors`
- `outcome`, if known

Attributes only from the existing `loom.*` allowlist plus the new ids #8664 already proposes. Must obey the epic's wire-safety rule: no prompts, generated code, raw tool arguments/output, keys or emails on the wire — this is a **summary**, not a transcript excerpt.

`session.analysis` (derived rollups: retry-loop detection, longest tool call, USD cost, anomaly flags) is explicitly a separate, later slice (sibling sub-issue, slice 5) — do not fold it in here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `session.summary` record kind exists, populated by the existing transcript-ingest pass, containing exactly the fields listed above (no prompt/tool-output/key/email content).
- [ ] The record is shipped through the exporter(s) configured via the G1 sink list (validate against at least one sink end-to-end; full multi-sink validation depends on the G1 sub-issue landing).
- [ ] `session.summary` rows for a day of daemon work are queryable (by role, model, repo) in whichever indexed backend is available for testing — per #8714's parent Acceptance, ClickHouse is the target once #8529's fixture manifest / the G1 sink applies.
- [ ] Extend the existing redaction tests to cover the new record kind: no prompt, tool output, key, or email ever appears on the wire for a `session.summary` record.

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/activity/transcript_ingest.rs` — existing transcript-ingest pass; extend to emit the new record kind alongside its current token-count-only reads
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/` — new record-kind definition, wherever `TelemetryEnvelope`'s existing record kinds are declared (exact module TBD — grep for the existing record-kind enum once scoping starts)
- Redaction test suite (exact file TBD — grep for the existing "no prompt/key/email on the wire" test, likely alongside `exporter.rs` or `otlp/`) — extend for `session.summary`
- `#8664`'s proposed new ids (referenced in this issue's own Proposal) — confirm exact attribute names before implementing, to avoid a second, incompatible id scheme

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: a fixture transcript produces exactly one `session.summary` record with the documented fields populated correctly (including a subagent transcript producing a record with `parent_session_id` set)
- [ ] Automated tests: extend the redaction test suite — assert no prompt, tool output, key, or email appears in a `session.summary` record for a transcript that contains all four
- [ ] Manual verification: once at least one exporter is configured, confirm a day's worth of `session.summary` rows are queryable by role/model/repo in the indexed backend available for testing

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

**Why `routine`, not `complex`**: this is a new, additive record kind emitted from an existing, already-instrumented ingest pass — the shape is fully specified by the parent issue and by existing schema (`activity.db`'s token counters), and a mistake (a missing field, a redaction gap) would surface in the redaction test or in a straightforward review of the record shape, not as a silent architectural regression.

## Related

- Parent: #8714 (observability multi-sink export)
- Sibling sub-issue: G1 multi-exporter (this slice rides its sink list to reach more than one backend)
- Sibling sub-issue: G3 `session.analysis` (later slice, derived from this record — do not fold in here)
- #8664 (interactive-session ids this record's attributes should reuse)
- #8529 (fixture manifest referenced by the parent's validation approach)

issues.title: Flaky test: role_runner shrinking_the_ring… fails on its random-draw precondition (OTLP job only, same commit passes elsewhere)
issues.body:
## Symptom

`role_runner::tests::shrinking_the_ring_reassigns_the_departed_hosts_slice_to_the_survivor`
fails non-deterministically on its **precondition** assert, not on the behaviour it
exists to pin:

```
thread 'role_runner::tests::shrinking_the_ring_reassigns_the_departed_hosts_slice_to_the_survivor'
panicked at loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs:5121:5
```

`loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs:5121` is:

```rust
assert!(!orphaned.is_empty(), "precondition: host 1 must have owned something to orphan");
```

## Evidence it is non-deterministic, not a real regression

Observed on PR #8662 at head `3bcd26eb2`, where **two jobs of the same CI run, on the
same commit, disagreed**:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| Rust Unit Tests (`process-per-test`) | 8123 run, **8123 passed**, 0 failed |
| Rust OTLP Feature Build & Test | 8190 run, 8189 passed, **1 failed** (this test) |

Run: https://github.com/rjwalters/loom/actions/runs/35776125577

The same job passed on that branch's base commit (`039725289`) on `main`
(run `35771235363`). PR #8662 touches only `.github/workflows/release.yml`,
`defaults/docs/release-cadence.md` and `loom-daemon/src/release_resolve/` — nothing
that can reach `role_runner`.

## Likely cause

The test is `#[serial]` and mutates global shard state via `ShardEnvGuard`, then builds
a 12-workspace fleet of `tempfile::TempDir`s and asserts that a 2-shard ring leaves at
least one of them **not** owned by host 0. Ownership is derived from the workspace path,
which is a randomly-named temp directory — so the precondition is a statement about a
random draw, and it is also exposed to whatever global env/shard state a neighbouring
serial test left behind. Both are enough to make the *precondition* (not the assertion
under test) fail occasionally.

## Suggested fix direction

Make the precondition deterministic rather than drawn: use fixed, known workspace paths
(or seed/choose paths until both shards are non-empty) so the test asserts the
reassignment behaviour it is named for, and never fails on the setup. Failing that,
assert the ring split up front and skip/retry the draw rather than panicking.

## Impact

A red `Rust OTLP Feature Build & Test` on healthy PRs — exactly the false red
`.loom/docs/ci-principles.md` calls out, and it blocks merges until someone
re-runs the job by hand.

---

## Curator Enhancement

Problem statement, evidence (two CI jobs on the same commit disagreeing), root-cause analysis, and suggested fix direction are already clear and well-argued. Verified the test exists exactly as cited: `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs:5110` (`shrinking_the_ring_reassigns_the_departed_hosts_slice_to_the_survivor`), with the precondition assert at line 5121 matching the panic message verbatim. `ShardEnvGuard` (line 4928) and the `#[serial]` attribute are present as described. `gh run view 35776125577` confirms the linked CI run's conclusion is `failure`. Duplicate check surfaced only unrelated cross-references (PR #8662, the same PR this issue's own evidence table cites — absorbed; and #8681, an unrelated docs-parity issue that only cross-references this one as an example of a different auto-label pattern — disregarded as out of scope).

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `shrinking_the_ring_reassigns_the_departed_hosts_slice_to_the_survivor`'s precondition (`orphaned` must be non-empty) can no longer fail on an unlucky random draw — either by using fixed/deterministic workspace paths, or by choosing/seeding paths until the ring split is guaranteed non-trivial before asserting.
- [ ] The behavior under test (reassignment of the departed host's slice to the survivor) is still exercised and still fails if that behavior regresses — the fix must not weaken the test into a tautology.
- [ ] The fix does not depend on evaluation order or leftover state from a neighboring `#[serial]` test (per the issue's own "Likely cause" section).
- [ ] Re-run the affected job (`Rust OTLP Feature Build & Test`) or an equivalent repeated-run harness enough times to gain confidence the flake is gone (a single green run does not prove non-determinism is fixed).

### Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/tests.rs` — the test itself (starts at line 5110), and `enabled_workspace()`/`ShardEnvGuard` (line 4928) if the fix changes how workspace paths or shard state are set up.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: the fixed test passes deterministically; run it repeatedly (e.g. `cargo test --workspace shrinking_the_ring -- --test-threads=1` in a loop, or via any existing flake-detection harness) to confirm the precondition no longer depends on a random draw.
- [ ] Automated tests: the full `role_runner::tests` module still passes under both the default and OTLP feature builds.
- [ ] Manual verification: confirm the fixed assertion still fails if the reassignment behavior itself is deliberately broken (i.e. the test still tests what it's named for).

<!-- loom:complexity=mechanical -->

Why `mechanical`, not `routine`: this is a self-contained test-only fix (no production code path changes) with an unambiguous verification method — a mistake is obvious from re-reading the diff, and correctness is directly checkable by running the test repeatedly.

issues.title: Auto-update: post-provision codesign check is unbounded and misreports a non-answer as a signature downgrade
issues.body:
## Bug Description

The post-provision signature-downgrade check in `defaults/scripts/cli/loom-daemon-update.sh`
(`verify_destination_artifact()`, around line 1235) has the same
"could not verify" vs "verified and it's bad" collapse that #8754 fixed one
layer up in `loom-daemon/src/release_fetch/signature.rs::verify_darwin` —
but in the shell, and with an additional unbounded-hang gap.

```bash
if [[ "$ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE_HAD_AUTHORITY" == "true" ]]; then
    ...
    dest_sig_desc="$(codesign -dvvv "$dest" 2>&1 || true)"
    if ! grep -q '^Authority=' <<<"$dest_sig_desc"; then
        err "Post-provision verification FAILED: ... Provisioning has DOWNGRADED the signature ..."
        exit 5
    fi
```

Two distinct problems:

1. **Unbounded.** There is no `timeout` around `codesign -dvvv`. On exactly
   the contended host that motivated #8754 (where `timeout 20 codesign -dvv
   /usr/bin/codesign` on a stock Apple system binary was observed to hang),
   this invocation hangs the update script indefinitely with no deadline and
   no diagnostic. Every other `codesign` invocation in the update path now
   runs under a deadline (`VERIFY_TIMEOUT` in `signature.rs`); this one does
   not.

2. **Misclassified if it does not answer.** `|| true` swallows any non-zero
   exit (including a `timeout`-induced 124, were one added), leaving
   `dest_sig_desc` empty. The `grep -q '^Authority='` then fails, and the
   script reports **"Provisioning has DOWNGRADED the signature"** and
   `exit 5` — an alarming, specific accusation about what provisioning did,
   produced by a `codesign` that never reported anything at all. This is the
   #8754 conflation verbatim: "we could not check" rendered as "we checked
   and it is bad".

Note that this check runs only when the pre-provision download demonstrably
carried an `Authority=` line (`ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE_HAD_AUTHORITY == "true"`),
which is precisely the case PR for #8754 still sets `had_authority:
Some(true)` for when only the `codesign --verify` call times out — so a host
under enough load to time out the Rust-side verify can reach this unbounded
shell-side `codesign` on the very next step.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Read `defaults/scripts/cli/loom-daemon-update.sh` around line 1226–1243
   (`verify_destination_artifact()`).
2. Confirm `codesign -dvvv "$dest"` carries no `timeout` wrapper, unlike the
   `codesign` invocations in `loom-daemon/src/release_fetch/signature.rs`
   (which run under `cmd_out::run_command(.., VERIFY_TIMEOUT)`).
3. Confirm that an empty `dest_sig_desc` — the state produced by any
   `codesign` that fails to print its report, for any reason — takes the
   `exit 5` "signature DOWNGRADED" branch rather than an inconclusive one.

## Expected Behavior

- The invocation runs under an explicit deadline (matching the rest of the
  update path's `codesign` calls).
- A `codesign` that does not complete produces an **inconclusive** result —
  a `warn` and a skip of the downgrade check, the same disposition the
  branch already uses a few lines above when `codesign` is not installed at
  all (`"'codesign' not available -- cannot verify the destination binary's
  signature survived provisioning"`) — not `exit 5` with a downgrade
  accusation.
- Only a `codesign` that **ran to completion** and reported no `Authority=`
  line may take the `exit 5` downgrade path.

## Actual Behavior

A `codesign` that hangs blocks the update script forever; a `codesign` that
otherwise produces no output causes the script to report a signature
downgrade that was never observed, and abort provisioning with `exit 5`.

## Impact

Same class and same host conditions as #8754 (a busy macOS host makes
`codesign` slow), one layer further into the update, with a worse failure
mode: an indefinite hang rather than a bounded abort, and an incorrect
accusation about what provisioning did to the binary's signature rather than
about the release artifact.

## Scope note

Out of scope for #8754, which is bounded to `verify_darwin` in
`loom-daemon/src/release_fetch/signature.rs` plus its test file. Filed
separately per Builder scope discipline while implementing #8754.

<!-- loom:premise-check exists=yes deliberate=no reversal=no verdict=clear -->
premise-searched: defaults/scripts/cli/loom-daemon-update.sh (verify_destination_artifact, the `codesign -dvvv "$dest"` call at ~line 1235 and the `ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE_HAD_AUTHORITY == "true"` gate at ~1226); loom-daemon/src/release_fetch/signature.rs (for the bounded-invocation contrast); grep for `codesign` across defaults/scripts confirms this is the only remaining unbounded one in the update path.

issues.title: Codex private-clone mode: persistent session workspaces and exclusive account leases
issues.body:
Part of #4489; extends the session-container implementation in #6896. First implementation step of the operator-requested private-clone path to routine daemon Codex.

## Problem and operator direction

A session container currently mounts the host workspace read-write at the same absolute path. That makes host worktrees accessible, but container execution alone does not isolate the host checkout, shared Git metadata, or sibling repositories. The inspected Studio session configuration on 2026-09-23 mounted the whole GitHub directory read-write.

The operator proposed one isolated repository copy per Docker container and then asked to queue this as the fastest path to Codex integration, deferring improvements. This is that explicit session direction, recorded by Codex; it is not an autonomous request to change all workers.

## Recommended implementation

Add an opt-in private-clone workspace mode to the existing persistent account session lifecycle. Keep the existing host-mounted mode available. Preserve one persistent account-owned authentication profile outside all repositories.

Use a Docker-managed persistent workspace volume owned by one account container. Prepare an independent clone of the configured forge repository inside it, with private Git metadata and objects; reuse it for subsequent jobs. Start from the resolved remote base revision and use existing issue-branch/worktree helpers entirely inside this private clone. Do not copy a dirty host checkout, use host Git alternates/shared object directories, or mount a writable host repository tree. Use private persistent build caches for this mode initially.

Acquire one exclusive job lease for the entire account session, covering every repository and both standalone roles and sweeps. Interactive repository-writing sessions must participate in this exclusion or cause admission to refuse. Different accounts may run concurrently.

Record enough secret-free identity to validate and recover the workspace: account, container identity, repository identity, private root, base revision, job owner and issue/branch. Unknown dirty or unpushed work must be retained and reported, never reset or removed just to make a slot reusable. A stale lease is reclaimable only after proving the old worker stopped; missing or ambiguous evidence remains unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Supported session start/status/stop interfaces expose the workspace mode and private-root identity; mismatched existing containers refuse reuse with an actionable migration instruction.
- [ ] A private-clone container has no host checkout or sibling-repository mount, no writable Git/object/cache sharing with another account, no container-runtime socket, and no privileged host escape.
- [ ] Clone/fetch use existing supported forge authentication without credentials in remote URLs, repositories, image layers or logs. The account authentication profile keeps its existing single-owner refresh semantics.

- [ ] Update the mount contract and session architecture documentation with this explicitly separate workspace mode, including private-cache placement and safe idle-container migration. Existing host-mounted mode retains its documented behavior.
- [ ] No daemon routing default or global Codex capability promotion changes in this issue.

- `docker/session/README.md` and `docs/adr/0017-session-container-architecture.md` — persistent authentication, headless execution, socket-free containment.

New lifecycle logic belongs in Rust behind the existing commands; keep the shell adapter thin.

No open code prerequisite. #8773 is merged via #8775; retain its supervised cancellation guarantees. The separate #8776 registry-lock fix is already being implemented and should not be duplicated.

Dispatch integration and capability admission follow in separate issues. Defer shared object caches, cross-account build-cache optimization, extra jobs per account and alternative container engines.

issues.title: champion-epic.md: the idempotency guard reads SKIP_STREAK from any marker-bearing comment, not just a rejection verdict
issues.body:
## Summary

`champion-epic.md`'s "Idempotency Guard for Unrevised Epics" selects the verdict
comment it reads `SKIP_STREAK` out of **purely by marker string**:

```bash
elif printf '%s\n' "$EPIC_JSON" | jq -e --arg m "$VERDICT_MARKER" \
       '.comments[] | select(.body | contains($m))' >/dev/null; then
  VERDICT_COMMENT=$(gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/$EPIC_NUMBER/comments" --paginate \
    --jq ".[] | select(.body | contains(\"$VERDICT_MARKER\"))" | jq -s 'last')
```

It never checks that the matched comment's own body actually says
`Champion Review: Epic Needs Revision` before deriving `SKIP_STREAK` (and hence
`UNREVISED_EVALS`) from it.

#7666 closed the *writing* half of this — `champion-epic-standdown.md` now writes
its own `champion:epic-tracking-umbrella:body-*` marker, and
`defaults/scripts/tests/test-champion-epic-verdict-marker-scope.sh` statically pins
the single-writer rule. The **reading** half is still marker-only, so a
**pre-#7666 stray** comment that already carries the reserved marker keeps
corrupting the ladder on epics that are still open today.

## Why the existing stray-marker backstop does not catch it

The guard's stray-marker branch keys on `PRIOR_REJECTIONS -eq 0`, and
`PRIOR_REJECTIONS` is a **whole-issue-history** count of
`Champion Review: Epic Needs Revision` comments — it does not care which body
revision they were posted against. So an epic that was rejected on an *old* body,
later fixed, and then had its **passing** verdict comment tagged (pre-#7666) with
the *new* body's reserved marker reads as:

- marker match (from the passing comment), **plus**
- `PRIOR_REJECTIONS >= 1` (from the old, superseded rejections), **plus**
- a `SKIP_STREAK` parsed out of the passing comment's own
  `champion:epic-unrevised-skips:<hash>:N` tally,

so `UNREVISED_EVALS = PRIOR_REJECTIONS + SKIP_STREAK` climbs past the cap and the
guard escalates a healthy epic that has never failed its *current* body's
evaluation.

## Live evidence

Observed on `rjwalters/kicad-tools` during a Champion pass (2026-09-23), filed
there as rjwalters/kicad-tools#5712:

- **#4410** — the comment matching the current body hash (`c01167674ddc243d`, id
  `5688541921`, posted 2026-09-15) is titled *"Champion Review: Epic Passes
  Evaluation — Already Decomposed, No Action Needed"*, not a rejection.
  `UNREVISED_EVALS` = 5 against a cap of 2.
- **#3438** — identical shape (`091e57a55577e9de`, id `5678899866`), carrying its
  own `champion:epic-unrevised-skips:...:3` tally.

Both epics are healthy and actively worked. Following the guard mechanically
would have parked both at `loom:operator-only` with an escalation comment claiming
"repeatedly failing structural criteria" — false, and it also removes them from
Step 0's completion-first check so they can no longer auto-close.

The stray markers themselves cannot be un-written; they are already posted on live
epics. The reader must be defensive about them.

## Proposed fix

Require the matched comment's **own body** to contain
`Champion Review: Epic Needs Revision` before treating it as a rejection verdict:

- filter the REST `VERDICT_COMMENT` selection on the rejection title as well as
  the marker, and
- widen the stray-marker branch so that a marker match with **no rejection-bearing
  comment behind it** takes the existing "no tally, no escalation, no comment"
  path, regardless of `PRIOR_REJECTIONS`.

A failed REST re-read (empty body) then also lands in the no-escalation direction,
consistent with #7965's fail-open rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guard cannot derive `SKIP_STREAK` / `UNREVISED_EVALS` from a comment
      that carries the reserved marker but is not a
      `Champion Review: Epic Needs Revision` verdict
- [ ] A marker match whose only marker-bearing comment is a passing/stand-down
      verdict takes the stray-marker path (no tally, no escalation, no comment)
      even when `PRIOR_REJECTIONS >= 1`
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/tests/test-champion-epic-verdict-marker-scope.sh` gains a
      fixture pinning exactly that shape, with a negative control so it cannot
      pass vacuously

issues.title: observability: capture all GitHub Actions runs/jobs of the 2amlogic org as OTLP telemetry via a loom-daemon ci-telemetry poller (SigNoz build/CI visibility, phase 1 of 3)
issues.body:
## What

Capture **every GitHub Actions run and job** of the `2amlogic` org as first-class OTLP telemetry from a new `loom-daemon ci-telemetry` poller. This is the foundation for standing build/CI observability in SigNoz: durations, outcomes, and per-run structure become queryable so we can retro on build/CI time regressions (motivation: build and CI times are currently felt but invisible — regressions only surface as "everything is slower").

Part of the SigNoz observability track (epic #8522): the transport (daemon OTLP exporter → neutral gateway → SigNoz) already exists; this issue adds the **CI source** that currently does not exist at all. Follow-on phases: full job-log capture with collector-side redaction (filed next), and SigNoz retro surfaces (filed next) — cross-linked at filing.

## Design (grounded in existing modules)

**New Rust module** `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/` + CLI subcommand `ci-telemetry` (per the shell-language policy: new executable logic is a daemon subcommand, not a `.sh`).

### CLI
- `loom-daemon ci-telemetry --once` — one poll cycle across the configured org; non-zero exit with a named reason on failure (a poll that cannot run must not look like a poll that passed — ci-principles rule 6)
- `loom-daemon ci-telemetry status` — ledger size, per-repo watermarks, last successful poll, records emitted/exported
- Daemon-integrated periodic poller when `autonomous.ciTelemetry.enabled=true` (default **false**, FLAGS-OFF; `LOOM_CI_TELEMETRY_*` env overrides, env > config > default via `config_resolver.rs`)

### Config block (`.loom/config.json` → `autonomous.ciTelemetry`)
| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` |
| `org` | `2amlogic` |
| `intervalSecs` | 120 |
| `excludedRepos` | `[]` |
| `logCaptureEnabled` | `false` (phase 2 flips it; must be a config gate, see scope) |

### Polling + dedup ("never do the same job twice")
- Discover repos via `GET /orgs/{org}/repos` (paginated, ETag/304-cached — the `forge_cached_list.rs` mechanism, never raw re-listing)
- Per repo: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs` with a `created_after` watermark from the ledger; for each unseen run → `GET /actions/runs/{id}/jobs`
- **Durable ledger** at `.loom/state/ci-telemetry/seen.jsonl`: append-only `(repo, run_id, job_id)` entries + per-repo watermark (latest observed `run.created_at`), fsynced before a record is emitted. A job is emitted **exactly once** regardless of restarts, re-polls, or re-runs. A crash between write and emit must never double-emit: the ledger write is the commit.
- Multi-host posture: polling may run on more than one fleet host, but records carry **stable identities** (`run_id`/`job_id` as the dedup key in attributes + local ledger) so a recipient can dedup; document the single-poller-as-normal-case assumption, per-repo lease coordination is explicitly out of scope unless fleet primitives make it trivial (one mechanism per behaviour — do not invent a second coordination layer)
- Rate limits: honour the existing rate-limit breaker; budget = repos × 2 request families per interval; a 403/secondary-limit backs off the whole org, not per-repo hammering

### Emission (through the existing `observability` OTLP exporter — no new transport)
- Record kinds: `ci.run` (repo, workflow, ref, head_sha, event, status, conclusion, triggered_by, started_at, completed_at) and `ci.job` (+ job name, runner label, attempts, timed_out) — mapped in `observability/otlp/mapping.rs` alongside the existing lifecycle kinds
- Metrics: `loom.ci.run.duration_ms` and `loom.ci.job.duration_ms` histograms; labels **only** `repo`, `workflow`, `job`, `runner`, `conclusion` (low-cardinality allowlist rule; never sha/ref/issue-number in metric labels)
- Traces: one trace per run, one span per job (parent/child like the sweep traces in `telemetry/trace/`), so Trace Explorer shows the CI waterfall
- **Local journal** `.loom/logs/ci-telemetry.jsonl` is written regardless of whether any exporter is configured (the `sweep-outcome-telemetry.jsonl` pattern) — the poller is useful offline

### Gateway allowlist
Extend `defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml` `keep_keys` with exactly the `loom.ci.*` attributes this phase emits; the fan-out contract test (`collector_fanout`) must assert each one. Nothing else admitted.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `loom-daemon ci-telemetry --help` documents the subcommand; building without the `otlp` feature still compiles (OTLP-gated paths behind the existing feature, like `exporter.rs`)
2. With a recorded-fixture GitHub API (wiremock-style or recorded responses, committed under the test dir — no live-network tests in CI), `--once` over a synthetic org with 2 repos × 3 runs × 4 jobs emits 2 `ci.run` + 3×4 `ci.job` records to the local journal with correct durations
3. **Idempotency (the money AC)**: a second `--once` over the same fixture emits **zero** records; killing the process mid-cycle and re-running emits each job exactly once total (ledger is the commit)
4. Unit tests cover: pagination continuation, `created_after` watermark advance, ETag 304 no-op on repo discovery, rate-limit backoff, ledger crash-recovery (torn trailing line is detected and repaired, not double-counted)
5. `status` distinguishes: never-polled / last-ok + age / failing + last error — silence never reads as healthy (house discipline)
6. `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` created (phase-1 section: config reference, dedup contract, local journal schema) with `.loom/docs/` parity copy (Docs/Defaults Parity Check must pass); `observability.md` map-of-docs table gains the row
7. Emitted metric label set and attribute allowlist match the collector `keep_keys` additions byte-for-byte (contract test)

## Explicit non-goals (this issue)

- **No job log download** — that is the follow-on phase; `logCaptureEnabled` exists as a gate that this phase must refuse to honour (config-gated off, named stub, no dead code that pretends to work)
- No re-hosting of GitHub's log UI, no per-step spans (job granularity is the unit)
- No per-repo lease/coordination protocol
- No changes to `sweep.*`/`tokens.*` record kinds

## Cross-links

- Epic: #8522 (SigNoz/ClickStack trial)
- Pipeline/transport docs: `.loom/docs/observability.md`, `.loom/docs/otlp-transport.md`
- Dedup/journal precedent: `.loom/docs/telemetry-schema.md` (local journal), #8669 (allowlist discipline)
- Policy home (follow-on issue): `ci-observability.md`

## Affected Files

- `loom-daemon/src/ci_telemetry/` (new module) - poller, dedup ledger, CLI subcommand
- `loom-daemon/src/observability/otlp/mapping.rs` - add `ci.run`/`ci.job` record mapping
- `defaults/observability/collector/config.yaml` - extend `keep_keys` with the new `loom.ci.*` attributes
- `defaults/docs/ci-observability.md` - add the phase-1 section (config reference, dedup contract, local journal schema) to the existing policy doc
- `defaults/docs/observability.md` - add the map-of-docs row
- `.loom/config.json` schema - new `autonomous.ciTelemetry` block

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: fixture-based `--once` run (2 repos × 3 runs × 4 jobs) asserts correct `ci.run`/`ci.job` record counts and durations
- [ ] Idempotency test: second `--once` over the same fixture emits zero records; kill-mid-cycle + re-run emits each job exactly once
- [ ] Unit tests: pagination continuation, `created_after` watermark advance, ETag 304 no-op, rate-limit backoff, ledger crash-recovery (torn trailing line)
- [ ] Contract test: emitted metric label/attribute set matches collector `keep_keys` additions byte-for-byte
- [ ] Manual verification: `loom-daemon ci-telemetry --help` / `status` output reviewed for the never-polled / last-ok+age / failing+last-error states

issues.title: merge-pr.sh: warn when a partial-increment trailer is backticked (the #3667 reset silently no-ops)
issues.body:
## Summary

`merge-pr.sh`'s partial-increment parser deliberately blanks inline code spans
before matching (#5234 — a backticked `Part of #N` is a hypothetical mention, not
a declared intent). That exclusion is correct. The gap it leaves is that a Builder
can write the convention's **exact** trailer text inside a code span — it reads as
"a literal piece of syntax, so put it in backticks" — and the PR then looks
completely right to a human reviewer and to Judge while silently defeating the
automation: `_partial_increment_refs` returns nothing, so the #3667
`loom:building` -> `loom:issue` reset no-ops with **no log line anywhere** and the
family/epic issue is stranded at `loom:building` indefinitely.

## Incident

Downstream on `rjwalters/kicad-tools`: merging PR #5686 into issue #5240, whose
body carried `` `Part of #5240` `` on its own line. The reset never fired; the
label swap and an explanatory comment had to be applied by hand. Filed there as
rjwalters/kicad-tools#5690; fixed there in PR #5692 (merged 2026-09-23) against
the **vendored** `.loom/` copies, pinned with a `.loom/resync-ignore` block whose
own comment says "unpin once the equivalent fix lands in rjwalters/loom's
defaults/ tree". Tracked there as rjwalters/kicad-tools#5693.

Two prior partial-increment merges on that same issue (#5649, #5488) used the
plain-text form and reset correctly — this is a body-shape trap, not a regression.

## Fix (detection, not a parser change)

Port the downstream fix into `defaults/`, so every consumer gets it and the pin
can be retired:

- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` — a non-blocking pre-merge warning
  (`_warn_backticked_partial_increment_trailers` plus two text helpers), in the
  same advisory style as the #4569/#4595 conflict warnings, called from
  `_check_partial_increment_close_conflict` **before** its empty-refs early
  return (the case it exists for is precisely the one where the ref list is
  empty). Pure text analysis, no extra forge calls.
- The matched shape is deliberately much narrower than the declaration anchor:
  the backticked trailer must be the **entire line** (modulo an optional
  list/blockquote marker, whitespace and one trailing punctuation mark), so the
  #5234 mid-sentence mention and a docs line listing trailers as examples stay
  silent, and fenced blocks are stripped first.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` — regression cases
  for the incident shape, the plain-text control, the #5234 prose control, docs
  prose, fenced blocks, the both-shapes case, list/numbered markers, and the
  `--dry-run` prefix.
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` — a "write the trailer as plain
  text, never backticked" caution next to the existing trailer example.

The `loom-daemon merge-pr-refs` parser is **not** touched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_partial_increment_refs`' answer for a backticked trailer is unchanged
      (still not a declaration)
- [ ] A whole-line backticked trailer emits a non-blocking warning naming the
      issue and quoting the offending line, and mutates nothing
- [ ] Plain-text trailers, mid-sentence backticked mentions, docs example lines
      and fenced blocks do not warn
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` passes

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

## Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` - add `_warn_backticked_partial_increment_trailers` (plus its two text helpers), called from `_check_partial_increment_close_conflict` before the `[[ -n "$partial_refs" ]] || return 0` early return (~line 1303)
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` - add regression cases: incident shape, plain-text control, #5234 prose control, docs prose, fenced blocks, both-shapes case, list/numbered markers, `--dry-run` prefix
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/builder-pr.md` - add a "write the trailer as plain text, never backticked" caution next to the existing `Part of #N` trailer example (~line 646)

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh` covers all cases listed in the Fix section and passes
- [ ] Manual verification: construct a PR body whose only partial-increment trailer is a whole-line backticked `` `Part of #N` `` and confirm `merge-pr.sh` (or its `--dry-run` path) prints the new non-blocking warning naming the issue and quoting the offending line, while `_partial_increment_refs` still returns nothing for it (AC #1 unchanged)
- [ ] Edge cases: verify no warning fires for (a) plain-text trailers, (b) mid-sentence backticked mentions (#5234 shape), (c) docs example lines, (d) fenced code blocks

issues.title: dashboard: host 'Degraded' trips on a single failed role tick or one load sample — nearly always on
issues.body:
## Problem

On dashboard.2amlogic.com, 3 of the 4 dispatching hosts render **Degraded** nearly all the time, while fleet throughput is healthy (2026-09-24: 108% of the 7-day merge average). Because Degraded is always on, the operator has learned to ignore it, so it no longer signals anything.

Snapshot of `GET /public/fleet-state` at 2026-09-24 ~20:05Z:

| host | tripped by | real? |
|---|---|---|
| loom-worker-1 | `roles.persistent`: `judge@loom x1` | no: loom commits judge=codex, workers have no codex account (296-tick skip streak) |
| loom-worker-2 | `dispatch_halted` (host breaker, load/core 3.5–3.9) + `judge@loom x1` | the halt is real and the breaker is doing its job |
| robb-studio | `roles.persistent`: 6 pairs, most from pool exhaustion | partly |
| robb-pro | nothing | ok |

## Why it is a hair trigger

`distressReason()` in `dashboard/web/src/fleet.ts` (origin/main ~L381; pinned deploy 25bf989f L347-364) returns a reason in any of these cases:

1. **`roles.persistent` is non-empty.** On the daemon side, `sample_role_tick_health` (`observability/collector.rs` ~L869) calls `summarize_role_ticks(records, DateTime::<Utc>::MIN_UTC)`. That means:
   - **There is no time window.** It scans the whole 2048-tick ring shared across every repo on the host. On a host with ~50 repos × 8 roles, that ring covers well over an hour.
   - **One failure is enough.** A (repo, role) pair counts as persistent if its *latest* tick failed. The existing `ROLE_TICK_ESCALATION_THRESHOLD` / `consecutive_identical` streak does not gate it.
   - A pair that failed once and then stopped ticking stays "persistent" until the ring evicts it or the daemon restarts.
   - With ~400 (repo, role) pairs per host, P(at least one latest-tick failure) is close to 1 at all times.
2. **`load_per_core >= 2.5` or `cpu_idle_fraction <= 0.02` from a single sample.** The comments call these a fallback for daemons that predate `dispatch_halted`, but they are evaluated unconditionally. One 5-minute spike marks a host Degraded even though the daemon's own breaker requires 3 sustained ticks (`DEFAULT_HOST_BREAKER_SUSTAIN_TICKS`).

## Proposed change

Dashboard side (preferred, no daemon change needed):

- **Role failures:** count a pair toward Degraded only if `consecutive_identical >= ROLE_TICK_ESCALATION_THRESHOLD` (or `failures >= N`) **and** `last_at` is within a recency window (e.g. 60 min). Keep showing sub-threshold failures as an informational line on the host card, but don't count them toward Degraded or "N need attention".
  - The `failures` / streak field has to survive `/public/fleet-state` redaction (`dashboard/src/redaction.ts` ~L392-430 keeps `failures` today; confirm it carries the streak and not a ring-total).
- **Load / idle fallback:** apply it only when the record has no `dispatch_halted` field (i.e. an old daemon). When `dispatch_halted` is present, it is the sustained, authoritative signal.
- **Optional:** exclude role failures whose cause is config-permanent and already surfaced elsewhere (e.g. a codex-pinned role on a host with no codex accounts). These could be reported as "misconfigured" rather than "degraded".

Daemon side (optional follow-up): pass a real `since` (e.g. now − 1h) instead of `MIN_UTC` in `sample_role_tick_health`, so `roles.persistent` means what its name says.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A host whose only role failure is a single failed tick (streak 1) renders **ok**, not Degraded.
- [ ] A host whose role pair has failed ≥ threshold consecutive times within the recency window renders Degraded, naming that pair.
- [ ] A host reporting `dispatch_halted: false` with a single-sample `load_per_core >= 2.5` renders ok. The same record without the `dispatch_halted` field still trips the fallback.
- [ ] `needsAttention` follows the new rule.
- [ ] Unit tests in the dashboard web suite cover all four cases above.

## Context

Found during a 2AM fleet check (operator: "the dashboard always seems to say our machines are degraded"). Deploys reach production only via the 2am `infra/dashboard/loom-ref` pin, which is currently 110 commits behind main.

issues.title: Route daemon Codex jobs into private clones with recoverable logs and checkpoints
issues.body:
Part of #4489 and the operator-requested private-clone workstream in #6896. Second implementation step.

## Problem

The Codex session adapter currently sends the host working directory and host workspace context to the container. Host status, worktree cleanup and sweep checkpoints likewise assume host-visible files. A private clone is not usable by the daemon until execution paths and retained job state are mapped explicitly.

## Recommended implementation

Wire the private-clone workspace and exclusive account lease from #8785 through the existing runtime/account selection and spawn-worker → spawn-codex → supervised session-exec path. Preserve the logical host repository identity for scheduling and reporting; resolve all child working-directory, project-root, worktree and hook paths to the private container workspace.

Prepare and verify the selected workspace before claiming an issue or starting model work. Hold the lease until worker termination is acknowledged, including descendants. Integrate with the #8773 cancellation protocol rather than inventing another lifetime mechanism.

Stream output through the existing host supervisor. Preserve the minimum durable checkpoint, branch/PR and artifact metadata needed for status, resume and cleanup through a narrowly scoped export/control interface. Do not regain file visibility by mounting host repositories or daemon control-state directories read-write into the worker.

Exchange code using the forge: fetch the configured base or resumable issue branch, push the issue branch, and create/update its PR through existing helpers. Any worktrees the role needs remain entirely inside the private clone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scheduled standalone roles and explicit/scheduled sweep launches use the same selected account, validated workspace and lease. All account paths respect one active job per account; unavailable/busy sessions yield an accurate reason and release temporary reservations.
- [ ] Child cwd, Loom context, installed helpers, guard bridge locations and runtime instructions resolve within the private clone. No stale host-absolute worktree path is passed as an executable child path.
- [ ] A credential-free integration fixture exercises the normal adapter chain through prepare, issue branch mutation, push/PR handoff, log capture and cleanup. Existing capability restrictions remain in force until #8787.
- [ ] Dashboard/status retain runtime, provider, account, logical repository, sweep/role identity and terminal outcome; logs remain accessible after cancellation or container loss without secret material.
- [ ] Daemon restart and worker interruption preserve checkpoints and branch/PR association. Unpushed work is retained; account failover must explicitly stop for recovery when the remote branch/checkpoint is insufficient to resume.
- [ ] Cancellation, host-supervisor death, failed startup, container disappearance and hung cleanup do not release a lease while a child can still write. Existing #8773 tests continue passing.
- [ ] Reapers and cleanup target the owned private workspace and lease, never the host's similarly named worktree. Cleanup/export inputs cannot select arbitrary host paths.

issues.title: merge-pr --auto (post-#8410): timeout reported as merge failure by Champion; duplicate --allow-unapproved audit comment; stale messages
issues.body:
Found while reviewing #8426 (#8410: `--auto` now settles checks and merges in-process). None of these blocked that PR.

## Observed

1. **A timeout is reported as a merge failure.** With #8426, `--auto` exits non-zero when CI outlasts `LOOM_AUTO_MERGE_TIMEOUT` (default 600s). The PR body calls that a retry on the next pass. However, Champion's error handling (`defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md`, the "Merge Failed" path) treats any non-zero exit as a failure and posts "a human will need to investigate". This repo's `Shell Test Suites (hermetic)` job alone takes about 10 minutes, so this is reachable, especially on the pass right after an exit-4 `--redate-stale-checks` re-run.
2. **Duplicate audit comment.** With `--allow-unapproved` and no `loom:pr`, `_revalidate_merge_guards` calls `_check_loom_pr_label` a second time after the wait. That posts a second "Merge Proceeded Without loom:pr" audit comment.
3. **Stale or misleading text.** `merge-pr.sh` still says "while auto-merge is disabled" in the settle-wait error path (around line 2066 at #8426's head). When the post-wait uncached re-read fails (`{}`), the refusal says the PR "does not carry loom:pr" rather than "could not re-read labels". It fails closed, which is correct, but the message sends the operator to the wrong fix.

## Suggested fix

(1) Give timeout its own exit code (or reuse exit 3's re-queue semantics) and document it in `champion-pr-merge.md`'s exit-code table. (2) Make the post-wait re-validation skip the audit comment, or de-dupe it. (3) Fix the two messages.

---

## Curator Enhancement

Verified all three observations against `origin/main` (current head, post-#8426 merge):

1. **Timeout-as-failure**: confirmed `merge-pr.sh`'s settle-wait timeout paths (e.g. `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh:2054`, `:2104`) call `error(...)`, which is `exit 1` (`merge-pr.sh:131`) — indistinguishable from a genuine merge failure. This repo already has precedent for a distinguished non-1 exit for a re-queue (not-a-failure) condition: exit 3 (`error_head_moved`, #5579) and exit 4 (stale-check re-date, #8508), both documented in `champion-pr-merge.md`'s "Exception: exit codes 3 and 4" section. A timeout fits the same shape and should get its own code in that family, with a matching exception carved into that doc section (do not follow the 5-step "Merge Failed" flow for it).
2. **Duplicate audit comment**: confirmed `_check_loom_pr_label` (`defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh:911`) posts the "Merge Proceeded Without `loom:pr` (Override)" comment whenever `--allow-unapproved` is set and `loom:pr` is absent, and it is called twice on the `--auto` path: once unconditionally at line 947 (pre-wait), and again from `_revalidate_merge_guards` at line 2222 (post-wait) — so with `--allow-unapproved` and no `loom:pr`, the comment is posted twice per merge.
3. **Stale/misleading messages**: confirmed `merge-pr.sh:2082` reads "...refusing to merge PR #$PR_NUMBER with failing check(s) **while auto-merge is disabled**" from inside the `if [[ "$AUTO_MERGE" == "true" ]]` block itself — contradictory now that #8426 made this the live `--auto` path. Also confirmed `_revalidate_merge_guards` (`merge-pr.sh:2200`) re-reads the PR via `forge_get_pr_nocache ... || echo '{}'`; on a failed re-read, `PR_LABELS` becomes empty and `_check_loom_pr_label` reports the loom-daemon guard's genuine-absence message (`loom_pr_guard.rs:110`, "does not carry the `loom:pr` label") — identical wording whether the label is truly absent or the re-read itself failed.

No duplicates found (`check-duplicate.sh --include-merged-prs --issue 8896`).

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The settle-wait timeout path (`defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` around lines 2054/2104) exits with a distinguished code (not the generic `error()` exit 1) analogous to exit 3/4, and `champion-pr-merge.md`'s "Exception: exit codes 3 and 4" section is extended to cover it (or renamed to include it) so Champion's operator-facing docs and behavior agree: do not post the "Merge Failed" comment or count it as an error for this exit.
- [ ] `_check_loom_pr_label`'s override audit comment is posted at most once per `merge-pr.sh --auto --allow-unapproved` invocation — either by skipping the post-wait re-check of this specific guard when the pre-wait check already posted the comment, or by de-duplicating the comment itself.
- [ ] The message at `merge-pr.sh:2082` no longer says "while auto-merge is disabled" inside the `AUTO_MERGE == true` branch.
- [ ] When `_revalidate_merge_guards`'s post-wait re-read of the PR fails (falls back to `{}`), the refusal names the re-read failure explicitly (e.g. "could not re-read PR labels after the settle-wait") rather than reusing the genuine-absence "does not carry the `loom:pr` label" wording — still failing closed, just with an accurate message.
- [ ] Existing merge-pr.sh test suites (settle-wait, loom:pr guard, head-moved/exit-3/exit-4 coverage) stay green.

### Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` — timeout paths (~2054, ~2104) for the new exit code; `_check_loom_pr_label` (~911) and `_revalidate_merge_guards` (~2200, ~2222) for the duplicate-comment fix; line ~2082's message text; the post-wait re-read failure message in `_revalidate_merge_guards`.
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md` — "Exception: exit codes 3 and 4 — head moved, re-queue, not a failure" section (~line 3317): extend to document the new timeout exit code and its own Champion handling exception.

- [ ] Manual verification: grep the updated `merge-pr.sh` for the corrected message text at both sites (no "while auto-merge is disabled" inside the `AUTO_MERGE` block; a distinct message for post-wait re-read failure vs. genuine label absence).

issues.title: forge_get_check_runs reads only the first 30 check-runs; merge-pr --auto's settle-wait cannot see the rest
issues.body:
Found while reviewing #8426 (#8410). Once that lands, `merge-pr.sh --auto`'s client-side settle-wait is the **only** check-settling mechanism: the server-side arm is gone.

## Observed

`forge_get_check_runs` (`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh`, the `gh api "repos/$nwo/commits/$commit/check-runs"` call) passes no `per_page` and no `--paginate`, so GitHub's default page size of 30 applies:

```
$ gh api repos/rjwalters/loom/commits/c53dcaa85860fe090be88d6c1d374cd59e5439b5/check-runs --jq '"\(.total_count) \(.check_runs|length)"'
39 30
```

This repo's CI produces 39 check-runs per head, so 9 are invisible to the settle-wait, both to its pending count and to its failed-required classification.

## Suspected impact (unverified)

The rows appear to come back newest first, so the long-running test suites are probably visible and the missing rows are early structural gates. The forge's own ruleset should still refuse a synchronous merge whose required checks have not passed, unless the merging identity has a bypass. That needs checking. This is present on `main` today; #8426 makes it load-bearing.

## Suggested fix

Add `per_page=100` and/or paginate. Also fail closed (treat as pending) when `total_count` exceeds the number of rows returned, so a future growth past any page size cannot silently shrink the checked set. Pin it with a test fixture where `total_count > len(check_runs)`.

Measuring that the missing rows never include a required check, and closing this with that evidence, is a valid outcome.

---

## Curator Enhancement

Confirmed on `origin/main` @ current head: PR #8426 ("merge-pr --auto settles checks and re-validates in-process instead of arming a server-side merge") **merged 2026-09-25T14:34:02Z** — so the scenario this issue flags as "once that lands" is now live, not hypothetical: `merge-pr.sh --auto`'s client-side settle-wait (`_wait_for_checks_then_sync_merge`, `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` ~line 2035) is the only check-settling mechanism today, and it relies entirely on `forge_get_check_runs` (`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh:652`), which still passes no `per_page`/`--paginate` to `gh api repos/$nwo/commits/$commit/check-runs` (line 690). Marking `loom:urgent` — this is a live gap in the mechanism this repo relies on to avoid merging PRs whose required checks have not actually passed (see CLAUDE.md § "CI is dumb and reliable, on purpose").

No duplicates found (`check-duplicate.sh --include-merged-prs --issue 8895`).

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `forge_get_check_runs` retrieves every check-run for a commit, not just the first page (add `per_page=100` and/or `--paginate` to the `gh api` call at `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh:690`).
- [ ] When the fetched row count is less than `total_count`, the caller fails closed (treats settlement as not-yet-reached / still pending) rather than silently trusting a truncated set.
- [ ] A regression test fixture exercises `total_count > len(check_runs)` and confirms the fail-closed behavior (per the issue's own Suggested fix).
- [ ] Existing `test-forge-helpers.sh` / `test-merge-pr-check-runs-404-fallback.sh` / `test-merge-pr-wait-for-checks-empty-settle.sh` suites stay green.
- [ ] Alternative closing condition (also acceptance-satisfying per the issue body): if investigation shows the missing rows can never include a required check (e.g. GitHub's check-runs endpoint is confirmed to always return required checks in the first page), document that finding with evidence and close without a code change.

### Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` — `forge_get_check_runs` (GitHub branch, ~line 690): add pagination and/or a fail-closed total-count check.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-forge-helpers.sh` — existing `forge_get_check_runs` coverage; extend or add a case for `total_count > len(check_runs)`.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-check-runs-404-fallback.sh` — exercises `forge_get_check_runs`'s distinguished exit codes; verify pagination changes don't disturb the 404/500/network-error paths.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-wait-for-checks-empty-settle.sh` — exercises the settle-wait loop's trust of a `forge_get_check_runs` read; extend for the truncated-page case if the fail-closed behavior needs loop-level coverage.
- `defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` — `_wait_for_checks_then_sync_merge` (~line 2035), the sole caller now that #8426 removed the server-side arm; reference only unless the fail-closed check needs to live here instead of inside `forge_get_check_runs`.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: existing forge-helpers and merge-pr check-runs/settle-wait suites stay green.

issues.title: Per-launch usage attribution and 429 bad-marking at the credential egress proxy (follow-up to #8674)
issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #8674 (credential egress proxy, epic #6896). The proxy shipped in the first
increment is, structurally, the **single choke point** every proxied provider request passes
through on its way off the host: it already parses the request head, knows the launch record,
and streams the whole response back. Two things #8674 listed as bonus effects fall out of that
position and are not implemented yet.

## Scope

**1. Per-launch usage attribution.** Record, per launch record, the request and response byte
counts and the provider's own rate-limit / usage response headers
(`anthropic-ratelimit-*`, `x-ratelimit-*`, `retry-after`, and the provider's token-usage
headers where it sends them). This is observed at the wire, at the moment it happens, rather
than reconstructed after the fact from retained logs — and it is attributable to one launch by
construction, because the launch record is what authorized the request.

Note: #8674's body cited #8563/#8564 as doing the "reconstruct from retained logs" this would
replace. Curator checked both and that citation does not hold (#8563 is closed Kimi-pool
onboarding; #8564 is session-level token/model attribution for the fleet feed). Treat the
attribution work here as new, not as a replacement for either.

**2. Bad-mark on quota exhaustion at the proxy.** When the upstream answers `429` or a
provider-specific quota-exhausted shape, the proxy can mark the pooled account bad
*immediately* — it holds the account identity (`credential::Resolved::{provider, account}`
travel into the record) — instead of waiting for the child to exit and for exit-code
inference to run.

Keep both strictly non-secret: the credential must never enter a counter, a log line or an
exported metric, and the placeholder is a live bearer token for the launch's lifetime, so it
must not be logged either. The existing `Record`/`Placeholder` `Debug` impls redact; anything
added here must keep that property.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-launch request/response byte counts and captured rate-limit headers are recorded for
      each proxied launch and surfaced somewhere durable (launch record / telemetry), keyed by
      `launch_id`.
- [ ] A `429`/quota-exhausted upstream response on a pooled API-key route bad-marks the
      selected account at the proxy, and the existing exit-code-driven path does not
      double-mark it.
- [ ] Nothing added logs, exports or persists either the real credential or the placeholder —
      asserted by a test, as the current suite does for `Record`/`Placeholder`.
- [ ] Unproxied (env-passthrough) dispatch is unaffected.

## Dependencies

- [x] #8674 / its implementing PR #8701: merged 2026-09-24 (PR #8701, `7a04dbbc`) — the
      `egress_proxy::{Record, Registry, server}` types this issue's attribution and

Dependency cleared — this issue is ready to build.

- `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/egress_proxy/server.rs` (lands with #8674/PR #8701) — add

- `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/egress_proxy/registry.rs` (lands with #8674/PR #8701) — extend

issues.title: noopCooldown is host-local (peer host re-dispatches inside the window), and the same release is also counted as a prless failure
issues.body:
## Problem

Two distinct defects in the accounting of a single no-op release, both observed
in one `loom-daemon` log for one issue, and both of which let a `noopCooldown`
window be ignored.

### 1. `noopCooldown` is host-local, so a peer host re-dispatches inside the window

`autonomous.workFinder.noopCooldown.cooldownSecs` defaults to 3600 and is
recorded into the recording host's own registry/`activity.db`. On a two-host
fleet sharing one repo, the peer host has no knowledge of it and re-offers the
candidate immediately.

Evidence — `~/.loom/daemon.log` on `loom-worker-*`, repo `2AMLogic/llm-cim`,
issue #1, 2026-09-25:

```
[06:38:29.656] [INFO] sweep_registry: issue #1 no-op release recorded via IPC
    (RecordNoopRelease, #6670): epic tracking container, no direct buildable work…
[06:38:29.656] [INFO] sweep_registry: issue #1 no-op-release cooldown armed —
    1 consecutive no-op release(s), next dispatch allowed in 3600s (#6670)
```

The issue's forge timeline then shows it re-claimed (`loom:issue` →
`loom:building`) at **06:41:45Z** — 196 s into a 3600 s cooldown — by a sweep on
the other host, and again at 10:34:18Z and 11:29:47Z. The recording host itself
honoured the window correctly and never re-dispatched; only the peer did.

This is the same class of problem `record-noop-release.sh`'s `--workspace-root`
default fixed for multi-*workspace* daemons (#6957) — one hop further out: the
cooldown is invisible across *hosts*, so on any multi-host fleet the effective
suppression is "one host stops trying" rather than "the fleet stops trying". The
lease-record mechanism (#6179) already establishes a forge-backed,
cross-host-readable channel for exactly this kind of shared claim state.

### 2. The same release is also counted as a `prless` **failure**

Immediately after the no-op cooldown was armed, the daemon classified the same
release as a PR-less failure:

```
[06:39:28.067] [INFO] sweep_registry: issue #1 dispatch backoff armed — 1 consecutive
    failed dispatch(es), next attempt allowed in 60s (#4485; cause=Generic)
[06:39:28.067] [INFO] sweep_registry: issue #1 insta-crashed (1/3 consecutive, <60s,
    no checkpoint) (#3939)
[06:39:28.067] [WARN] sweep_registry: issue #1 released without a pull request
    (1/3 consecutive) — next dispatch allowed in 300s (#7972). Failure: sweep exited 0
    after 213s without opening a pull request, without a phase checkpoint, and without
    a `.no-changes-needed` marker
```

So one release simultaneously armed a 3600 s no-op cooldown **and** a 300 s
prless-retry window and an insta-crash strike. The two paths disagree about what
happened, and the *shorter* window is the one whose semantics are wrong for this
outcome.

The stated discriminator is the `.no-changes-needed` marker, and the daemon
reports it absent — yet the orchestrator clearly took the no-op path (it issued
`RecordNoopRelease`). Either the sweep records the no-op without writing the
marker `sweep.md` step 1 reads from, or the daemon looks for the marker somewhere
the sweep did not write it (e.g. the wrong worktree root, or after the worktree
was reaped). Whichever it is, a self-reported no-op should not also accumulate
insta-crash strikes toward quarantine.

## Suggested fix

1. Make a no-op cooldown visible fleet-wide, not just host-locally — e.g. publish
   it alongside the lease record (#6179) or via the peer-coordination channel the
   registry already uses to re-advertise live peer claims (#4431), so a peer host
   yields the same way it yields to a fresh peer lease.
2. Make the no-op and prless-failure classifications mutually exclusive for one
   release: if `RecordNoopRelease` arrived for the issue in this dispatch, suppress
   the prless-failure/insta-crash accounting instead of arming both. Separately,
   reconcile the marker check with whatever the sweep actually writes, so the
   discriminator the code relies on is the one the orchestrator produces.

Context: `2AMLogic/llm-cim#105` (a ~12-session thrash loop on `loom:epic`
containers). Related: #8881 (Mode A/B pre-flight has no `loom:epic` skip rule),
#8911 (find-work tiers 1/2 bypass the configured skip labels).

## Problem

Split out of #8914, covering the second finding in the comment on that issue. **In-place re-runs of stale required checks can still lose to a busy `main`.**

The #8248 freshness guard treats **any** base-tip move after a required check started as making that check's green result stale. On 2026-09-25 `main` moved at 14:26, 14:47 and 14:58 UTC, and each move landed before a full CI run (about 8 min) finished. PR #8641 lost the race three times, including twice with operator in-place re-runs.

#8914 reduces the window. It re-runs only the stale **required** jobs, in place, and merges as soon as they are fresh. There is a platform limit, though. Verified 2026-09-25: GitHub allows **one** job re-run per workflow run at a time, and a second `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` in the same run returns `403 "The workflow run containing this job is already running"`. All 19 required contexts on `main` live in the single `ci.yml` run, so they are re-run one after another, at roughly 12–20 s each (a few minutes in total). That is much shorter than the full run, but it is not zero.

## Candidate directions (need a design pass, possibly an operator decision)

1. **Input-aware staleness.** A base move whose diff touches no ratchet/baseline file and no input of any required check does not make the checks stale. This narrows #8248's "any move" rule, so it needs a precise definition of "required-check input" and must fail closed when that input set can't be determined. #8248's incident (a baseline tightened under an in-flight PR) must stay covered.
2. **Put the required checks in their own fast workflow.** If the required ratchet/lint jobs lived in a separate workflow (for example `required-checks.yml`), a single whole-run re-run (`POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun`) would refresh all of them in parallel in about 1 minute, instead of one job at a time inside `ci.yml`. This is a CI restructuring, so check it against `ci-principles.md`.
3. **Merge serialization.** Have Champion hold off merging other PRs while one PR's in-place re-run is in flight.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A design decision is recorded for which of these (if any) to pursue.
- [ ] Any change to #8248's staleness predicate keeps the 2026-09-18 incident timeline refused (see `stale_checks/tests.rs`).

Related: #8914, #8248, #8508, #8641.
