issues.title: bug(runtime): spawn-generic-launch.sh resolves the tier-3 manifest from cwd instead of the REPO_ROOT it already computed
issues.body:
## Summary

`defaults/scripts/spawn-generic-launch.sh` (added by #8695, closing #8671) resolves `REPO_ROOT` from its own `SCRIPT_DIR` but does not pass it to the `runtime-launch-env` subcommand, so tier-3 launch-shape resolution falls back to the daemon's **current working directory** while runtime *admission* for the same dispatch resolves against the **scripts-derived** root.

Surfaced during Judge review of #8695. Not a regression, and not a reason the PR was held — filing as a suggestion.

## The divergence

`spawn-generic-launch.sh`:

```bash
REPO_ROOT="$(git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"   # line 72
BIN="$(loom_daemon_self_bin_override || loom_locate_daemon_bin "$REPO_ROOT")"
...
LAUNCH_ENV="$("$BIN" runtime-launch-env --runtime "$RUNTIME_NAME" 2>&1)"           # line 78 — no --repo-root
```

`REPO_ROOT` is used only to locate the binary. With `--repo-root` omitted, `RuntimeLaunchEnvArgs::run` falls to `find_worktree_root_from_cwd().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."))`.

On the other side, `loom-daemon/src/worker_spawn/mod.rs` resolves `let root = workspace(args.scripts_dir.as_deref())?` and hands *that* to `runtime_admission::resolve_and_admit(root, ...)`, and spawns the adapter with `Command::new(runner)` — no `.current_dir(...)`, so the child inherits whatever cwd the daemon had. The same `<name>.json` is therefore read against two different roots in a single dispatch.

## Reproduction

With a custom tier-3 manifest at `.loom/runtimes/<name>.json`:

```
$ (cd "$REPO" && loom-daemon runtime-launch-env --runtime zzprobe)      # rc=0, resolves
$ (cd "$REPO/loom-daemon/src" && loom-daemon runtime-launch-env ...)    # rc=0, resolves
$ (cd /tmp && loom-daemon runtime-launch-env --runtime zzprobe)         # rc=1
runtime-launch-env: no runtime manifest found for "zzprobe" at ./defaults/runtimes/zzprobe.json (and no bundled fallback)
```

## Why it is low severity today

- `aider`, the only shipped tier-3 runtime, has a bundled compiled-in manifest, so its resolution is cwd-independent. Verified: a full `spawn-worker.sh` dispatch against a mock `aider` emits `--yes-always --message hello world` identically on #8695's head and on `origin/main`.
- In the normal sweep dispatch the worker's cwd *is* the worktree, so the two roots coincide.
- `RuntimeLaunchEnvArgs`' own doc comment shows the cwd default was a deliberate choice for the linked-worktree case, citing `repo_root::find_worktree_root`.

## Why it is still worth closing

1. **Silent wrong value.** A repo that customises `.loom/runtimes/aider.json` (e.g. pinning a different `cliBin`) gets the *compiled-in* manifest instead, with no diagnostic, whenever cwd is outside the repo. Customisation is the stated point of the installed-mirror precedence.
2. **Misleading diagnostic.** A *custom* tier-3 runtime in the same situation has no bundled fallback, so it takes the exit-78 refusal that names the `requires-daemon: runtime-launch-env >= …` version floor — blaming a stale binary when the actual cause is cwd. That refusal is otherwise well-built; this is the one input that makes it lie.
3. **Precedent.** `03bd5d007` / #8540 ("resolve the registry explicitly instead of from cwd") landed two commits below #8695's base for exactly this bug class.

## Suggested fix

Pass the already-computed root:

```bash
LAUNCH_ENV="$("$BIN" runtime-launch-env --runtime "$RUNTIME_NAME" --repo-root "$REPO_ROOT" 2>&1)"
```

This is strictly more robust than the cwd default — inside a linked worktree `SCRIPT_DIR` is `<worktree>/.loom/scripts`, so `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` yields the worktree root, matching what the cwd default produces in the case it was designed for, while also being correct when cwd is elsewhere. If the cwd default is preferred for some case not covered here, the alternative is to make `worker_spawn` set the adapter child's `current_dir` to the `workspace()` root so the two resolutions cannot disagree — but one of the two should happen.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Launch-shape resolution and runtime admission resolve `<name>.json` against the same root for a given dispatch.
- [ ] A custom `.loom/runtimes/<name>.json` is honoured regardless of the invoking cwd.
- [ ] Regression coverage in `defaults/scripts/tests/test-spawn-generic-launch.sh`: a manifest-declared `cliBin` still reaches argv when the script is invoked with cwd outside the repository.
- [ ] Existing 18/18 and 48/48 suites stay green.

## Secondary note (same file, cheap to fold in)

~~Line 78 captures `2>&1`, merging stderr into the string handed to `eval`.~~ **Already fixed on `main`, unrelated to this issue's own fix**: commit `9e88522ff` ("fix(runtime): don't eval runtime-launch-env's stderr", a Doctor pass on #8695's own branch before it merged) switched this to a stdout-only capture with a `# stderr is NOT eval'd` comment. No Builder action needed for this note — it's listed here only for history.

## Dependencies

- [x] PR #8695: merged — **verified 2026-09-26** via `git show origin/main:defaults/scripts/spawn-generic-launch.sh` (file exists) and `git log --oneline -- defaults/scripts/spawn-generic-launch.sh` (landed in `7ceec3dc7`, "merge train C: #8899 #8823 #8939 #8904 #8962 #8949 #8695 (#8996)", 2026-09-25T22:08:38-07:00). Note: the GitHub API reports PR #8695 as `state: CLOSED`/`mergedAt: null`, not `MERGED` — this repo batches several PRs' commits into one "merge train" PR (#8996) and closes the originals individually, so `CLOSED` here means "landed via the train," not "rejected." Confirmed the actual file content on `origin/main` directly rather than trusting the PR's own merge state.

This issue is now unblocked — `defaults/scripts/spawn-generic-launch.sh` exists on `origin/main` and a Builder can proceed.

## Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/spawn-generic-launch.sh` — pass `--repo-root "$REPO_ROOT"` to the
  `runtime-launch-env` call. **Re-verified on `origin/main` @ `7ceec3dc7`, 2026-09-26**: the call
  is still line 78 (`LAUNCH_ENV="$("$BIN" runtime-launch-env --runtime "$RUNTIME_NAME")"  #
  stderr is NOT eval'd`) and still omits `--repo-root` — the fix described in Suggested Fix above
  is unchanged and still needed. Do NOT also touch the `2>&1` capture — that part of the
  Suggested-fix snippet is now stale; stderr separation already landed (see Secondary Note above).
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-spawn-generic-launch.sh` — add the regression case from Acceptance
  Criteria: a manifest-declared `cliBin` reaches argv when invoked with cwd outside the repository

## Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: new regression case in `test-spawn-generic-launch.sh` — cwd outside the
      repo, custom `.loom/runtimes/<name>.json`, confirm the manifest's `cliBin` still reaches
      argv (AC3)
- [ ] Automated tests: existing 18/18 and 48/48 suites (per this issue's own AC4) stay green
      after the fix
- [ ] Manual verification: reproduce this issue's own repro steps
      (`cd /tmp && loom-daemon runtime-launch-env --runtime <custom>`) before and after,
      confirming the failure is resolved
- [ ] Edge cases: confirm `aider`'s bundled compiled-in manifest resolution is unaffected (it
      doesn't depend on `--repo-root` today, but the change must not break its
      cwd-independent fallback)

issues.title: worktree node_modules symlinks the primary clone, so pnpm's purge prompt invites deleting it
issues.body:
## Summary

`worktree.sh` symlinks a new worktree's `node_modules` at the primary clone's. That makes `pnpm run <script>` unusable inside the worktree: pnpm's pre-run dependency check decides the modules directory needs re-provisioning, tries to purge it, and aborts without a TTY —

```
ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY
Aborted removal of modules directory due to no TTY
If you are running pnpm in CI, set the CI environment variable to "true"
```

The message names its own workaround, and that workaround is the problem: `CI=true` tells pnpm to proceed with removing a directory that **belongs to the primary clone**, from inside a worktree, for a repo that shares one `node_modules` across every worktree.

## Observed

Every worktree in the affected repo:

```console
$ ls -ld .loom/worktrees/*/node_modules
.loom/worktrees/issue-200/node_modules -> /Users/.../rulehunt/node_modules
.loom/worktrees/issue-209/node_modules -> /Users/.../rulehunt/node_modules
.loom/worktrees/issue-215/node_modules -> /Users/.../rulehunt/node_modules
```

A Builder hit this running the repo's required pre-PR check (`pnpm run ci`) from its worktree and worked around it by invoking `npx tsc` / `npx biome` / `npx vitest` directly. It flagged the reason explicitly: pnpm "wants to purge it — which would delete the main repo's `node_modules`".

I did not verify whether `CI=true` actually deletes through the symlink or merely replaces the link, because that is not a thing to test destructively on a working clone. Either outcome is bad: deleting the target breaks every worktree and the primary checkout at once, and replacing the link silently gives one worktree a private `node_modules` while the others still point at a directory that no longer matches the lockfile they were installed from.

## Why it matters beyond one repo

The failure lands on the **documented happy path**. Loom's Builder workflow is "claim issue → `worktree.sh <N>` → implement → run the repo's checks → open PR". Any repo whose check script is a `pnpm run` target hits this on every single issue, and the error text actively recommends the dangerous flag. An agent that follows the message's own advice does the destructive thing.

It is also silent in the other direction: because the worktree shares the primary clone's `node_modules`, a branch that changes dependencies is tested against the *primary clone's* installed tree, not its own. A PR that adds or bumps a dependency can pass locally for reasons unrelated to its own lockfile.

## Suggestions

1. **Make the symlink safe to use, or do not create it.** If the intent is disk sharing, a pnpm-aware arrangement (a shared store with a per-worktree `node_modules`, which is what pnpm's content-addressable store already exists to provide) gets the space saving without the aliasing.
2. **If the symlink stays, guard the destructive path.** A worktree-local `.npmrc` with `confirmModulesPurge=false` would turn the abort into a refusal-to-purge rather than an invitation to force it.
3. **Document it in the Builder role.** Until it is fixed, `builder.md` should say plainly: inside a Loom worktree, do not run `pnpm install` or `CI=true pnpm ...`; invoke binaries directly. Right now nothing warns, and the pnpm error steers the reader the wrong way.

Related: #8927 (stale `loom:blocked`). Both are cases where the tooling's default path produces a wrong outcome quietly.

issues.title: Admit Codex mutable roles using verified private-clone containment
issues.body:
Part of #4489; third implementation step in the operator-requested private-clone workstream. #4496 remains the production evidence gate.

## Problem

Independent repositories prevent a container worker from damaging a shared host checkout, but the daemon currently admits Codex from a static capability manifest where worktreeIsolation is partial. The adapter additionally requires managed native hooks for mutable roles. Merely removing the host mount would therefore still leave Builder, Doctor and full sweeps unusable.

The operator requested isolated copies as the fastest integration path, with optimization deferred. Implement a distinct, verified execution context; do not globally declare native Codex hook parity complete.

## Recommended implementation

Extend admission so private-clone containment can satisfy the repository-isolation requirement for a launch whose account, container, mounts, private Git root and exclusive job lease are validated. Carry the validated context through account selection and spawn, and recheck its identity at execution. A configuration flag, environment variable or container label alone is insufficient evidence.

For this mode, the whole private clone is the worker's owned repository sandbox; local disposable base-checkout edits are not host-main edits. Existing issue branches/worktrees remain the workflow. Explicitly document this scope of isolation so it is not mistaken for native per-worktree hook parity.

Reconcile the adapter's mutable-role preflight with that context. Replace only the filesystem-isolation obligation covered by independent clones. Inventory the remaining obligations of the existing hook bridge—protected remote branch mutations, destructive actions outside the owned workspace, Loom lifecycle controls and credential boundaries—and retain or provide an enforceable mechanism for each. A Docker boundary does not prevent an authenticated force-push. Where a required policy is unproven, refuse with the precise remaining requirement rather than silently waive all hook checks.

Keep ordinary host/shared-mount Codex admission unchanged. Record execution-specific capability provenance in diagnostics and status. Support the already selected runtime preference order without altering repository-specific preference or scheduled-role settings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Builder, Doctor and sweep-lifecycle admission can use verified private-clone isolation through the normal runtime path. Read-oriented roles keep their existing requirements; every path still checks remaining role capabilities.
- [ ] Bare-host, host-repository-mounted, shared-Git, shared-account-lease and unverifiable sessions remain refused for the new containment claim. Missing/stale container identity and a mount/lease change between preflight and launch fail closed.
- [ ] Global Codex hooks/worktreeIsolation values are not changed to yes based on this feature. Admission records distinguish verified clone containment from native hook parity.
- [ ] The managed-hook preflight is explicitly reconciled with clone mode; there is no unconditional skip flag, trust bypass, test-only environment variable or prompt-only policy standing in for enforcement.
- [ ] Tests prove allowed private issue-branch edits/commit/push and denial of host/sibling/peer-repository writes, arbitrary host control/executor access and protected-remote destructive operations using disposable local fixtures.
- [ ] Preserve workflow/credential protections and test the actual launch path, including attempts via shell, patch, helper and any supported secondary mutation channel. Do not claim container isolation makes credentials or forge operations harmless.
- [ ] Update the runtime/guardrail documentation with an obligation-to-mechanism table, supported image/CLI/protocol versions, evidence requirements, remaining limitations and rollback to the prior runtime.
- [ ] Automated tests cover both explicit Codex selection and capability-aware fallback. No change silently makes an unverified Codex account eligible or falls through from an explicit runtime pin.
- [ ] Prepare the private-clone test matrix for #4496, including an actual daemon-dispatched bounded full lifecycle after disposable-repo success. Mock/CI evidence cannot satisfy the live go/no-go; do not enable fleet defaults here.

## Implementation starting points — curator must verify

Verified against origin/main at 135183d9b2527cb2cc81d2c5d8e0ba1f2213c645:

- `loom-daemon/src/runtime_admission.rs` — full sweeps are a single runtime launch checked against Builder requirements.
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/runtime_preflight.rs` and `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs` — capability-aware selection and dispatch.
- `defaults/runtimes/codex.json` — partial native capabilities and their live evidence requirements.
- `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` — mutable-role hook readiness gate.
- `defaults/docs/guardrail-parity-codex.md` — current hook bridge covers filesystem, destructive-command and workflow policies.

Use Rust for execution-context verification and admission; keep one shared decision path.

## Dependencies

- [x] #8785 — private workspace and exclusive lease; merged in #8800.
- [x] #8786 — normal daemon launch, recovery and observability inside that workspace; merged in #8830 (`d678331b6`).
- [ ] #8839 — protected private-session guard code/policy/hook-registration boundary (Builder-discovered 2026-09-24: mid-session edits to `.loom/config.json` or the bridge disable force-push denial; mutable admission must consume this boundary).

Existing #8256/#8322 cover tool-policy infrastructure and should be reused where applicable; they are not a reason to widen this issue into a policy-engine rewrite. Required missing protection discovered during curation must be named concretely.

<!-- loom:premise-check exists=yes deliberate=yes reversal=no verdict=clear -->
premise-evidence: defaults/runtimes/codex.json — native Codex isolation remains partial pending its own evidence gate.
premise-evidence: loom-daemon/src/runtime_admission.rs:1 — mutable full sweeps intentionally require Builder capabilities.
premise-extends: add an evidence-backed containment mechanism for the explicitly selected private-clone execution context; preserve native capability truth, existing host/shared-mount refusals, and the requirement to satisfy every applicable safety obligation.

## Curator implementation handoff — 2026-09-24

<!-- loom:complexity=complex -->

Verified against `origin/main` at `e86b361c1`. The former dependency holds are resolved. This is a security-sensitive admission change, not a capability-manifest promotion. Keep the original acceptance criteria above as the completion contract.

### Verified corrections

- #8786 now provides `tokens_pool::private_workspace::dispatch::Selection`, which owns the selected account and exclusive lease. Preparation validates actual Docker settings/mounts/ownership and runs outside the sweep-registry lock. `transport::run` adopts the inherited open file description, checks the durable job/container identity again, and launches by container ID. Reuse these mechanisms; do not introduce a second account-selection pass.
- Capability rejection currently occurs **before** that preparation in `sweep_registry/private_dispatch.rs`; preference selection also rejects Codex using the static manifest. The worker independently repeats static admission in `worker_setup::execute`. Updating only `runtime_admission.rs` or only the shell adapter will therefore leave a broken or inconsistent path.
- `worker_setup::setup` installs the managed hook bridge, but successful installation is **not proof of hook trust or policy readiness**. It currently reports setup ready without a final trusted-hook verification. The mutable adapter preflight remains a separate enforcement obligation.
- #8256 and #8322 are still OPEN. Their proposed role-tool-policy module is absent from this build base. Existing managed guards are available; do not import assumptions about the unmerged #8314 implementation or make this issue a general role-policy rewrite.
- The session image pins Codex `0.149.1` (`docker/session/Dockerfile`), while the bridge documentation/schema pin is `0.146.0`. The implementation must document and test the supported combination instead of treating the CLI minimum version as protocol evidence. The current private transport protocol is `loom-private-workspace-v1`.

### Implementation sequence

1. Introduce an execution-specific admission context whose construction requires the validated `Selection`/lease. Keep configuration parsing, inventory checks and status probes unable to manufacture this proof. Override only the repository-isolation requirement covered by the private clone; continue checking every other role requirement and retain the static API's refusals for ordinary host/shared sessions.
2. Thread context and provenance through explicit selection, the capability-aware preference walk, scheduled roles, unlocked sweep preparation, adapter preflight and worker execution. Explicit pins never fall through. Drop rejected candidates' temporary leases/reservations; keep Docker work outside scheduler/registry locks. Revalidate the bound container, mounts, private Git root and lease immediately before execution.
3. Reconcile managed hooks narrowly. Retain verified/trusted enforcement for remote-operation and Loom-workflow policy; clone containment cannot replace those guards. No fabricated trust receipts, blanket bypass flags or environment-only containment claim. If the tested CLI/policy combination cannot enforce a required rule, return that precise unmet obligation before claiming work.
4. Record context/provenance in diagnostics and durable status without credentials or raw operator configuration. Preserve recovery ownership and the existing prohibition on automatic private account/runtime failover. Update the guardrail/private-dispatch docs and the #4496 test matrix; leave production runtime defaults unchanged.

### Obligation → mechanism to preserve and prove

| Obligation | Existing base / required work |
| --- | --- |
| Host, sibling and peer repository isolation | Actual Docker mount/security inspection, private named volume and independent Git root, exclusive account/volume ownership. Bind this evidence to admission and recheck at launch. |
| Exclusive writer and stale-context refusal | Owned lease descriptor plus durable job/container identity; preserve #8786 cancellation/recovery behavior and test preflight-to-launch changes. |
| Protected remote operations | Managed destructive-command policy, or another demonstrated enforceable mechanism. Docker/network availability alone is insufficient. Verify protected remote refs remain unchanged after denied force-push/deletion attempts. |
| Loom lifecycle controls | Retain managed workflow guards for merge/helper and control mutations. Private `run-job` refusal and MCP/plugin/profile audit already restrict host control; preserve them. |
| Credential boundary | External per-account profile, narrow selected mounts/environment and redacted outputs. The selected profile and forge access remain sensitive; prove peer profiles and exported records cannot expose credentials. |
| Control/guard integrity | The clone is writable and its current helpers/bridge resolve inside it. Before relying on that bridge for admission, demonstrate how edits to policy/config/guard files cannot silently disable required enforcement; refuse an unproven path. |
| Secondary mutation channels | Cover shell, patch and helper calls through the actual launch. Preserve denial of unsupported channels such as `write_stdin`; MCP/plugin/control audit is not permission to introduce another unguarded executor. |

### Affected files / test entry points

All existing on the verified build base; new verifier modules may be added beside these:

- `loom-daemon/src/runtime_admission.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/runtime_preference.rs` and `runtime_preference/resolve.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/role_runner/runtime_preflight.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/private_dispatch.rs`
- `loom-daemon/src/tokens_pool/private_workspace/{dispatch,transport,worker_setup,control,docker,lease,export}.rs`
- `defaults/scripts/spawn-codex.sh` and the existing managed hook/provisioning boundary
- `loom-daemon/tests/private_workspace_docker.rs` and its `dispatch.rs`/`auth.rs` fixtures
- `defaults/docs/guardrail-parity-codex.md`, `defaults/docs/private-session-dispatch.md`, `docker/session/Dockerfile` (version contract reference)

### Verification plan

- Shared Rust admission tests: Builder/Doctor/sweep-lifecycle, unchanged read roles, an additional unmet capability, missing proof, explicit Codex refusal without fallback, and Claude → verified Codex → Z.ai preference selection. No promotion of global partial capabilities.
- Disposable Docker tests through production `SweepRegistry::dispatch_unlocked` and `ScriptRoleInvocationRunner`, then the real adapters/supervisor/worker: allowed issue edit/commit/push plus required denied operations above. Do not substitute a synthetic freeform selection for actual mutable-role admission.
- Negative variants: host/shared Git/mount, peer profile or volume attachment, busy lease, changed/replaced container, stale/missing identity and mutation between preparation and launch. Assert refusal before model/claim where appropriate and inspect filesystem/remote refs afterwards.
- Reuse the complete Linux daemon and existing UID-1000/public-source CI fixture. Run Docker tests with their normal parallel execution as well as focused failures; preserve profile permissions. All credentials/remotes/accounts must be disposable synthetic fixtures.
- Check structural/shell/version gates, relevant Rust tests and Clippy, then PR CI and the required post-merge gate. Real authenticated daemon-dispatched lifecycle evidence remains #4496, after disposable success; CI does not establish the production go/no-go.

## Problem

`defaults/scripts/cleanup-branches.sh` reuses `merge-pr.sh`'s `_maybe_delete_local_branch` for its `pr-*` review-branch pass. It `awk`-extracts the function body out of `merge-pr.sh` and `eval`s it, alongside:

- a `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/branch-landed.sh"`, plus a hand-written fail-closed `branch_landed()` shim for a partially-resynced `.loom/`;
- the extracted transitive helpers `_primary_worktree_path`, `_is_primary_worktree_path`, and `_find_worktree_by_branch`, plus fallback shims for each.

The #8191 local-branch-cleanup slice turned `_maybe_delete_local_branch` into a thin call to `loom-daemon merge-pr delete-branch`, which is the same `worktree_cli::branch_delete` rule `worktree.sh remove` uses. After that slice, **none of the sourced/extracted helpers above is called by the extracted body.** They are dead weight in the portable-shell pool. The extract-and-`eval` contraption also exists only to avoid a second implementation. That goal is now met more directly by calling the subcommand itself.

That slice intentionally left `cleanup-branches.sh` unchanged. Its retained suite `test-cleanup-branches-pr-review-branch.sh` asserts on that wiring's source text in 9 places, and changing it would have widened the slice beyond the `merge-pr.sh` port.

## Suggested fix

- Replace the extract/`eval` block with a direct `loom-daemon merge-pr delete-branch --repo-root … --branch … --expected-head-sha … [--default-branch …]` call. Replay its `LEVEL<TAB>message` stdout through the script's own `info`/`warning`/`success`, as `merge-pr.sh` does. Or, better, add a small shared shell helper both callers use.
- Drop the `branch-landed.sh` sourcing, the `branch_landed()` shim, and the dep-helper extraction list.
- Retire the source-text assertions in `test-cleanup-branches-pr-review-branch.sh` under the three-part test in `defaults/docs/verification-recipes.md` §6, with the suite's behavioural cases as successors. Those cases already run against the pinned daemon.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cleanup-branches.sh` no longer extracts or `eval`s any function from `merge-pr.sh`.
- [ ] `test-cleanup-branches-pr-review-branch.sh`'s behavioural cases pass unchanged. Any retired source-text assertion is recorded via `retired()` with a named successor.
- [ ] The portable-shell line count drops, and nothing in the file-size / shell-budget ratchets grows.

Surfaced while reviewing #8951 (the Pi `usage_source` reader). This is a follow-up suggestion, not a blocker for that PR.

## Observed

The source-scan tests `pi_usage::tests::the_only_file_open_in_this_module_is_the_guarded_log_reader` (#8951) and `codex_usage::tests::the_only_file_open_in_this_module_is_the_guarded_rollout_reader` (already on `main`) pin "never read a credential-bearing file" by counting lexical idioms in the module's comment-stripped source. I ported the Pi scan's exact string logic to Python and ran it against mutated copies of `loom-daemon/src/pi_usage.rs` (this was an emulation, not a cargo run):

| Mutation appended to `pi_usage.rs` | Scan result |
|---|---|
| `std::fs::read_to_string(p.join("auth.json"))` | FAIL (caught) |
| `std::fs::read_dir(p)` | FAIL (caught) |
| `p.join(".pi").join("agent").read_dir()` + `std::fs::File::options().read(true).open(..)` | **PASS (missed)** |
| `crate::codex_usage::tokens_by_model(p, None)` (delegating to another module's reader) | **PASS (missed)** |

Missed idioms:
- `Path::read_dir()` in method form. Only `fs::read_dir(` is counted.
- `File::options()`. Only `OpenOptions` and `File::open(` are counted.
- `".pi"` as a path segment passed to `join`. Only `.pi/` with a slash is forbidden.
- Crate-internal readers such as `walkdir`, `glob`, or another `*_usage` module's public reader.

The codex scan is weaker still. It has no `read_dir` entry and no forbidden-name list.

## Suggested hardening (unverified; the scope is for the Builder to decide)

- Add `.read_dir(`, `File::options`, `WalkDir`, and `glob(` to the zero-count idiom lists in both tests.
- Forbid the quoted segment `".pi"` (and `".codex"` for the codex reader) in addition to `.pi/`.
- Optionally forbid `crate::` paths into other reader modules, or accept that delegation is out of a lexical scan's reach and say so in the test's doc comment.

The behavioral tests (`a_refused_path_is_never_opened_even_when_it_holds_a_valid_stream`, `read_rollout_refuses_an_unauthorized_path_even_when_handed_one_directly`) already cover a gate that stops returning. This issue is only about the lexical scan's coverage.

issues.title: check-runs reads outside forge_get_check_runs can still truncate (Gitea branch, daemon stale-checks guard)
issues.body:
Found while implementing #8895 (PR #8986), which fixed the GitHub branch of `forge_get_check_runs` (`per_page=100` + `--paginate`, plus a fail-closed rc when the row count is short of `total_count`). Two other reads of the same endpoint class were deliberately left out of that PR's scope.

## 1. `forge_get_check_runs`, Gitea branch

`defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` — the Gitea branch makes ONE unpaginated request:

```
gitea_api GET "repos/$FORGE_OWNER/$FORGE_REPO/commits/$commit/statuses"
```

Gitea caps a page at `MAX_RESPONSE_ITEMS` (50 by default, `DEFAULT_PAGING_NUM` 30), so the same 30-row truncation class applies. Worse, this branch derives `total_count` from the rows it received (`total_count: (. | length)`), so the fail-closed short-read check the GitHub branch now has is structurally unable to fire here — a truncated read looks self-consistent.

The library already has `_forge_gitea_paginate` (used by `forge_get_pr_reviews`), which fails closed on a pagination failure and refuses to report a truncated list. Restructuring this branch to use it (per-row jq filter + `jq -s` to rebuild the `{total_count, check_runs}` rollup) is the fix. Note `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` is at its file-size baseline (1011 code lines), so the change must be line-neutral or shrinking.

A `KNOWN GAP (Gitea)` comment on the helper's doc block points here.

## 2. `fetch_check_runs` in the daemon's stale-checks guard

`loom-daemon/src/merge_pr/stale_checks/fetch.rs` (~line 226) passes `per_page=100` but does **not** paginate, and its `--jq` drops `total_count` entirely, so there is nothing to compare a row count against:

```rust
&format!("repos/{nwo}/commits/{head_sha}/check-runs"),
"--method", "GET", "-f", "per_page=100", "--jq",
"[.check_runs[]? | {name: .name, status: .status, conclusion: .conclusion, started_at: .started_at, app: .app.slug, details_url: .details_url}]",
```

Less acute than #8895 (100 is above this repo's 39, and this feeds the stale-checks guard rather than the settle decision), but it is the same silent-subset shape: a repo that grows past 100 check-runs gets a guard evaluated on a subset with no signal that anything was missing. Fix shape: paginate, and keep `total_count` so a short read can fail closed the way the shell helper now does.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Gitea branch of `forge_get_check_runs` retrieves every commit status for a commit (not one page), and a pagination failure returns nonzero rather than a short list.
- [ ] The daemon's `fetch_check_runs` paginates and fails closed (error, not a partial `Vec<CheckRun>`) when the retrieved count is short of the endpoint's `total_count`.
- [ ] Regression coverage for each: a multi-page fixture, and a short-read fixture asserting the fail-closed path.
- [ ] `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` does not grow past its file-size baseline.

Either half is independently shippable; splitting into two PRs is fine.

---

## Curator Enhancement

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

Verified both gaps against `origin/main` @ `7e0a29b0d` (2026-09-27) — both match this issue's description exactly, no drift since filing. See curator comment below for the verification detail (file-size baseline, enumeration of other call sites, duplicate check).

### Affected Files

- `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` - Restructure the Gitea branch of `forge_get_check_runs` (~line 561-590) to page through `commits/{sha}/statuses` via the existing `_forge_gitea_paginate` helper (already used by `forge_get_pr_reviews`) instead of one unpaginated call, and derive a real `total_count`/short-read check the way the GitHub branch already does (line 606-638) — line-neutral or shrinking overall, since the file is at its 1011-line baseline.
- `loom-daemon/src/merge_pr/stale_checks/fetch.rs` - Add pagination (mirroring the shell helper's `--paginate` fix from #8895) to `fetch_check_runs` (~line 269), and keep `total_count` through the `--jq` projection so a short read can fail closed instead of silently returning a `Vec<CheckRun>` subset.

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated tests: add a multi-page Gitea `statuses` fixture (more rows than one page) asserting `forge_get_check_runs` returns the full merged set, not a truncated first page.
- [ ] Automated tests: add a short-read fixture for the Gitea branch (fewer rows returned than the forge's own count implies) asserting the function fails closed rather than returning a self-consistent-looking partial result.
- [ ] Automated tests: add equivalent multi-page and short-read fixtures for `fetch_check_runs` in `fetch.rs`, asserting pagination and a fail-closed error (not a partial `Vec<CheckRun>`) on a short read.
- [ ] Manual verification: run `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh`'s existing test suite (if any) plus `cargo test` in `loom-daemon` for the `merge_pr::stale_checks` module after the change.
- [ ] Verify `defaults/scripts/lib/forge-helpers.sh` line count has not grown past its `scripts/file-size-baseline.txt` entry (1011 lines).

issues.title: feat(dashboard): visual timeline dashboard for Loom lifecycle and token usage over time
issues.body:
<details>
<summary>Original issue (preserved)</summary>

### Problem Statement
Operators currently lack an at-a-glance web view on the Loom dashboard (`https://dashboard.2amlogic.com`) to visualize token throughput (tokens/min), % capacity saturation, and end-to-end issue lifecycle progression.

### Proposed Solution
Add interactive time-series plots and lifecycle waterfall views to the web dashboard backed by local OTLP/SigNoz metrics.

---
**Operator Priority Bump** (comment by @2ambots, 2026-09-26): Promoted to `tier:goal-advancing` and `priority:high` by @turian via Chat-Ops.

</details>

---

<!-- loom:complexity=routine -->

## Curator Enhancement

### Problem Statement (clarified)

The operator's framing names a concrete target: **`dashboard.2amlogic.com`**. That
hostname is **not** the embedded `loom-daemon serve` HTML dashboard (the
loopback-only, port-7420, no-build-toolchain page compiled into the daemon
binary — see `.loom/docs/daemon-reference.md` §"Fleet dashboard"). It is the
**reference deployment of the `dashboard/` Cloudflare Workers app**
(`loom-observability-backend` — ingest + D1 history + a `FleetState` Durable
Object + the Phase-3 UI in `dashboard/web/`), confirmed by `CHANGELOG.md`
("Reference deployment: dashboard.2amlogic.com") and `WORK_LOG.md` ("2AM
production deploy: dashboard.2amlogic.com cutover", issue #4859). All work
below targets `dashboard/web/src/`, not `loom-daemon/src/serve.rs`.

**Correction to the original "Proposed Solution":** it says the dashboard is
"backed by local OTLP/SigNoz metrics." That's a different, parallel effort —
SigNoz/ClickStack/HyperDX is a *separate* telemetry trial (epics #8522/#8529,
`.loom/docs/observability.md`, `ci-observability.md`) with no wiring to
`dashboard.2amlogic.com`. The dashboard's actual data path is
`loom-daemon`'s own native `HttpsExporter`
(`loom-daemon/src/observability/exporter.rs`) pushing to the Workers
`/ingest` route, not OTLP/SigNoz. This issue's work has no dependency on the
SigNoz effort.

**This dashboard already has substantially more built than the issue as filed
implies.** Before scoping work, here is what already exists (epic #4702,
issues #4726/#4750/#4751/#4752/#4753/#4847/#4998/#8852):

- **Per-sweep lifecycle timelines** (`web/src/sweepTimelineView.ts` +
  `timelineBuilder.ts`, issue #4750): phase progression
  curator → builder → judge → doctor → merge, per sweep, with durations and
  PR link.
- **Historical charts** (`web/src/historicalChartsPanel.ts`, issue #4751):
  outcomes-over-time, success-rate trend, duration percentiles — full
  interactive charts (dated axis, hover tooltip, accessible table fallback)
  via `web/src/charts/chartChrome.ts`.
- **Per-host sweep-throughput and health-trend charts**
  (`web/src/hostHistoryPanel.ts`).
- **Token/cost analytics** (`web/src/analytics/*`, issue #4752): per-account
  burn curves (`burn.ts`), exhaustion forecasts including a computed
  **burn-rate `slopePerHour`** (`forecast.ts`), per-repo attribution
  (`attribution.ts`), and — **already rendering today, on both the
  authenticated and public surface** — a **"Fleet token-pool load" panel**
  (`web/src/analytics/render.ts`'s `renderPoolBurn`/`renderPoolBurnCard`)
  that draws a small SVG **sparkline of peak/mean `usage_fraction` (i.e. %
  pool capacity) over time, per host, 0–100%-pinned**
  (`renderPoolSparkline`).
- A CPU/load **saturation badge** per host (`idle`/`elevated`/`critical`,
  issue #4998, `src/publicPage.ts`) — a *different* kind of "saturation"
  (CPU load, not token/dispatch capacity).

So the literal phrase "% saturation UI panel" for token usage is **partially
already shipped** as a decorative sparkline. What is genuinely missing, and
what this issue should scope to, is narrower than the original title
suggests.

### What's actually missing (the real gap)

1. **No rolling *rate* (throughput) visualization exists anywhere.**
   `forecast.ts` computes `slopePerHour` (usage_fraction consumed per hour,
   least-squares fit over the live burn segment) purely to project an
   exhaustion ETA — it is never plotted as its own time series. There is a
   ready-made formatter for it (`analytics/format.ts`'s `formatRatePerHour`
   → `"N.N%/h"`) but no chart.
2. **The existing pool-load sparkline is decorative, not a first-class
   chart.** It is a bare inline SVG (`renderPoolSparkline`) with no dated
   x-axis, no hover tooltip, and no `renderTableView` accessible fallback —
   unlike the three real charts in `historicalChartsPanel.ts`, which all use
   `charts/chartChrome.ts` for exactly that chrome.
3. **"Tokens/min" is not a representable unit.** Per
   `dashboard/docs/token-analytics.md` (§"Units are limit-window
   fractions"): *"No absolute token count or price exists anywhere in the
   telemetry, so none is synthesized."* `tokens.snapshot` (see
   `.loom/docs/telemetry-schema.md`) carries only `usage_fraction` (a
   fraction of a rolling rate-limit window) per account, never a raw token
   count. Any "rolling token throughput" panel must be honestly labeled as a
   **burn *rate*** (`%` of pool capacity per hour), not tokens/minute — the
   operator's Chat-Ops phrasing ("tokens/min") does not match what the data
   model can support, and the panel must not imply a unit it cannot back.
4. **No dispatch/concurrency-capacity saturation view.** `queue.snapshot`
   (schema v11, `.loom/docs/telemetry-schema.md`) already carries
   `max_concurrent` (the concurrency cap a tick ran under) and
   `counts.running`, and — like every ingested record — is persisted
   unconditionally to D1 by `handleIngest` in `dashboard/src/index.ts`
   (regardless of `kind`), so `running / max_concurrent` over time is
   *already queryable* via `/api/history`/`/public/history` with **zero
   backend changes**. This is a second, orthogonal "% capacity saturation"
   signal (compute/dispatch capacity, not token-pool capacity) and is
   explicitly **out of scope** for this issue (see Overlap note below).
5. **No fleet-wide multi-sweep "lifecycle waterfall".** The existing
   `sweepTimelineView.ts` renders one sweep's phase list at a time. A
   Gantt/waterfall view of *concurrent* sweeps across the fleet (the
   original issue's "Proposed Solution" language) is a materially larger UI
   feature than a single chart.

### Overlap with sibling issue #9032 (being curated in parallel)

#9032 ("expose dedicated org-wide ranked ready dispatch queue view
`/dashboard/queue`") targets the **same repo directory** and, notably, a
route (`/#/queue`) that **already exists**: `web/src/views/workQueue.ts`'s
`workQueueView` already renders a live running/ready/blocked queue at that
hash route (issue #8852, phase 3), backed by `queue.snapshot` — though
#9032's proposed backend (`GET /api/v1/queue/ranked`, a fresh org-wide
GitHub-issue ranking by `work_finder::candidate_cmp`) is not obviously the
same data source. Whoever curates/builds #9032 needs to reconcile that
overlap; it is out of scope for #9029 to resolve. **For this issue:** do not
touch `web/src/views/workQueue.ts`, `web/src/workQueue.ts`,
`web/src/queueTypes.ts`, or the `#/queue` route — the chart this issue adds
lives in `web/src/analytics/` and/or `web/src/charts/`, a disjoint file set.

### Acceptance Criteria (single-PR core)

Build **one** new chart: a **rolling token-pool burn-rate ("throughput")
chart** — the genuinely net-new piece named in the operator's framing.

- [ ] A new derivation function (e.g. `web/src/analytics/burnRate.ts` or
      added to `burn.ts`) computes a **bounded rolling-window rate** (%
      pool-capacity-per-hour) from `PoolBurnCurve`/`PoolBurnPoint` data
      (`web/src/analytics/burn.ts`), reusing the existing segment
      boundaries (`buildPoolBurnCurves`' rollover/gap segmentation) so a
      limit-window reset never reads as a throughput cliff or a fabricated
      negative rate.
- [ ] The rolling window is a named, bounded constant/option (no unbounded
      in-memory accumulation) — consistent with the existing
      `DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS` / `CHART_PAGE_SIZE` bounding pattern in
      `web/src/historicalChartsPanel.ts`.
- [ ] A new chart-view module renders the rate series as a **first-class
      interactive chart** using `web/src/charts/chartChrome.ts` (dated
      x-axis, y-axis, hover tooltip, `renderTableView` accessible
      fallback) — matching `web/src/charts/successRateChartView.ts`'s
      pattern, not a bare decorative sparkline like the existing
      `renderPoolSparkline`.
- [ ] The panel/axis/labels call the metric a **burn rate** (`%/h`, reusing
      `analytics/format.ts`'s existing `formatRatePerHour`) — never
      "tokens/min" or any absolute token count.
- [ ] Renders on **both** the authenticated (`/api/history`) and public
      (`/public/history`) surfaces, matching the existing pool-level
      public-exposure precedent in `docs/token-analytics.md` (§2): pool
      aggregate fields (`mean_usage_fraction`/`max_usage_fraction`/
      `exhausted_count`) are already public-safe. The new chart must **not**
      introduce any per-account or per-repo identity onto the public
      surface — no changes to `src/redaction.ts` should be needed; if the
      implementation finds it needs one, that is a sign the metric chosen
      is per-account, not pool-level, and the design should be revisited.
- [ ] No changes to `dashboard/src/index.ts` (ingest), `src/query.ts`, D1
      migrations, or `src/redaction.ts` — every input this chart needs is
      already ingested and queryable today.
- [ ] New unit tests for both the rate-derivation function and the
      chart-view render, following the existing pairing convention
      (`web/test/successRate.test.ts` + `successRateChartView.test.ts`),
      including a test asserting a limit-window rollover does not produce a
      spurious large-negative rate point.
- [ ] `npm --prefix dashboard test` and `npm --prefix dashboard/web test`
      (or the repo's `npm run check:all` in `dashboard/`) pass. **Do not run
      `cargo` anywhere for this issue — it is a TypeScript/Workers-only
      change.**

### Explicitly out of scope (documented follow-ups, not filed as issues)

1. **Upgrade the existing decorative pool-load sparkline**
   (`renderPoolBurn`/`renderPoolSparkline` in
   `web/src/analytics/render.ts`) to the same `chartChrome.ts` chrome as
   the new rate chart — arguably the more literal reading of "% saturation
   UI panel", but deliberately deferred so this PR stays to one new chart.
2. **Dispatch/concurrency capacity saturation** (`queue.snapshot`'s
   `counts.running / max_concurrent`, per-host and fleet-wide, over time) —
   a second, legitimate "% capacity saturation" signal, already fully
   queryable historically with zero backend changes. Deferred to avoid
   `web/src/views/workQueue.ts` file overlap with #9032 until that issue's
   scope settles.
3. **Fleet-wide multi-sweep "lifecycle waterfall" / Gantt view** — the
   original issue's "lifecycle waterfall" phrase. Materially larger than a
   single chart; `sweepTimelineView.ts` only covers one sweep at a time
   today.
4. **Live SSE-driven auto-refresh** of the new chart (the existing
   `HistoricalChartsPanel` pattern re-fetches `/api/history` on filter
   change, not via the live event tail in `sseFeedClient.ts`) — nice-to-have,
   not required for acceptance.

### Affected files (expected)

- `dashboard/web/src/analytics/burn.ts` or a new `analytics/burnRate.ts` —
  rate derivation
- `dashboard/web/src/analytics/render.ts` — mount the new chart alongside
  the existing pool blocks
- A new `dashboard/web/src/charts/*ChartView.ts` (or an `analytics/`-local
  equivalent) reusing `charts/chartChrome.ts`
- `dashboard/web/test/*` — new test files per the pairing convention above
- `dashboard/docs/token-analytics.md` — document the new rate metric next
  to the existing burn-curve/forecast documentation (small doc update, same
  file the existing burn-curve public-exposure decision already lives in)

### Test Plan

- [ ] Automated: unit tests for rate derivation (including the
      segment-boundary/rollover case) and for the chart-view render
      (following `successRateChartView.test.ts`'s structure).
- [ ] Manual: `npm --prefix dashboard run dev`, seed a host with a few
      `tokens.snapshot` samples spanning a rollover (see the `README.md`
      "Local development" `curl` recipe), confirm the new chart renders on
      both `/` (authenticated) and the public variant without per-account
      data leaking into the public response.
- [ ] Edge cases: fewer than 2 samples in range (no chart / explicit
      no-data state, not a crash); a rollover mid-window; a multi-host pool.
